title: Yahoo Fantasy with Josh: "32 Teams. 32 Fantasy Football Facts to BULLY Week 8" (Stats vs. Film)
summary: In Week 8 Stats vs. Film (2:27, Josh, Hayden and Matt), all three hosts say Luther Burden gains the most from Kmet's injury. They're cool on Jonah Coleman, Hayden calls Corum near an RB2 when the Rams are favored, and they think JT's outlook worsened after the Colts sold Nelson and Buckner. Josh calls Garrett Wilson a buy (Hayden doesn't) and Antonio Williams the most under-discussed asset. For Poncho: MAIN still has an **empty FLEX and K**, so Caleb Douglas belongs in that FLEX. DYNASTY has Questionable Tyler Warren in a FLEX (Rachaad White is the swap) and an empty K. In HE-MAN'S HEROES, start James Cook now that BUF is off its bye and find a TE for Kittle's bye. In SUPERFLEX, activate Lamar if he's cleared. The Yahoo files are 3 days old.

disagreements.text: Jonah Coleman: Hayden ("everyone likes him more than I do") and Josh (won't "prop him up") are both cautious; Matt allows a "moderate hit." Not a true split, but all three are below the waiver-show consensus (BDGE/O'Hara, Joel Smyth).
Garrett Wilson: Josh says buy; Hayden says WR20 ROS and that buying now is buying from people selling low — he isn't calling it a buy.
Josh Jacobs vs JT: Hayden would "rather have Jonathan Taylor" but it's close; Josh says Hayden is higher on Jacobs than he is and is "terrified" of GB's rushing attack.
KC's WR fix: Matt prefers Josh Downs (knows the plays faster); Hayden calls Downs redundant with Rice and pitches Keenan Allen.
Saquon: Matt and Josh buy his "I'll play" claim; Hayden says the team is "extremely desperate," so he'll play through it.

takeaways: Burden is the Kmet-injury winner. All three hosts agree; CHI likely goes to more 11 personnel. Loveland stays a TE1.
The Broncos backfield is a three-way split. The Yahoo crew is the coldest room on Coleman this week.
Corum is a real flex when the Rams are favored (W8 vs LAC, LAR 26 projected); Kyren still leads when they trail.
JT's outlook got worse without Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner; Hayden would rather see him traded. IND is projected for 19 at JAX.
Zay Flowers + Lamar (Rapoport said Lamar plays; Sleeper still shows Out) is Hayden's WR5 for the week.
Caleb Douglas is MIA's WR to own; Willis is a streamer after this week.
Garrett Wilson split: Josh buys, Hayden ranks him WR20 ROS.
Skattebo is the lead back with Tracy on IR, but NYG is on bye in W8.
NE: Henderson is droppable (24% snaps), and Rhamondre is a sell.
Antonio Williams is the WAS piece to own coming off the bye; Diggs stays part-time.

title: Sal Vetri: "7 Players About to GO NUCLEAR in Fantasy (Trade For Them Now)" — Week 8 buy-low video
summary: Sal's Wednesday buy-low video (22:07, solo) names seven trade targets: **Chuba Hubbard** (ROS #28; he'd even trade Bijan or Jaylen Warren for him), **Jalen Coker** (#43, WR1–2 at ~14–15 PPG), **Christian Watson** (#20, still a 2nd-round WR despite Golden), **A.J. Brown** ("value has never been lower"; Wk8 is his expected 100% return), **Jonah Coleman** (overbid FAB; 50% snaps on his debut, Payton wants him more involved), **Germie Bernard** (26% share, Pittman maybe done for the year), and **DJ Moore** (32% share in full games, into the top 50 if he practices). For you: Coker is Questionable ahead of Thursday at GB in MAIN. Sal says to shop **Jordan Mason** in MAIN and SUPERFLEX. He's neutral on **Jacobs** vs Hubbard in HEROES, and he'd move **Shaheed** for Coker (DYN and HEROES). In DYN, Freddy is starting Bernard, one of Sal's buys.

segments.title: Cold open: halfway point, trade deadlines approaching, "trade for them as soon as possible"
Chuba Hubbard (and CAR as a whole): the irony of his earlier sell calls, the "market" framing, 33 scoreless yards in the blowout, usage dip explained, efficiency ranks, ROS #28, trade examples

Jalen Coker: the overthrown 48-yd TD (via Hartitz), YPRR rank, 27% share when on the field with McMillan, 3 healthy games, a WR1–2 projection of 14–15 PPG, ROS #43, trade examples, and all three Thursday-night
Christian Watson: two stinkers, Love's 274 yds with drops, GB spreads it out, Golden's 30% share vs Watson's 20%, YPRR ranks, the center injury, Love's 35–40 attempts, ROS #20
DraftKings ad (promo code SAL)
A.J. Brown: 0 usable weeks, Jeff Mueller's "Week 8" reminder, high-ankle explanation, 94% routes, 27% share, CeeDee Lamb comparison, Maye "MVP," ROS #36, sell package
Jonah Coleman: overbid on FAB, Wk7 usage (11 touches, 50% snaps, 41% carries, 34% routes), Dobbins and Harvey's season lines, Payton's quote, the Hartitz pre-draft chart, ROS #149 "moving up a lot"
Subscribe plug ("over 50%" of viewers aren't subscribed)
Germie Bernard: 3/27 dud, Rodgers check-downs (9 of 19 completions to RBs), 26% share over 3 weeks, Wk9 bye, Kaboly on Pittman possibly out for the season, ROS #85, trade examples
DJ Moore: shoulder history, 17% season share vs 32% in completed games, Wk1 5/100/1 (38% share) vs HOU, Wk3 6/67 (30%), BUF #1 in points per game, ROS #58 moving into the top 50
Wrap and plug for the panic video

tone: Salesman-calm and contrarian: "it's like a market." He openly owns the irony of buying Panthers he told you to sell early in the season. He's patient and gives A.J. Brown "some grace." The only urgency is his push to overbid FAB on Coleman.
confidence (1\u20135): A.J. Brown 5 ("value has never been lower"); Hubbard 4–5; Coleman 4; Watson 4; Coker 4; Bernard 3 (bye caps it); DJ Moore 3 (practice-dependent).
bullish: Hubbard, Coker, Watson, Golden, Jordan Love's volume, A.J. Brown, Maye, Coleman, Bernard, DJ Moore, Josh Allen and BUF's offense.

title: "WR Rest of Season Rankings I Week 8 Fantasy Football trade targets"
hosts: solo. Mentions Theo Gremminger (asks viewers to hype the Theo ROS bold-predictions video instead of this one)
an upcoming BTBS ROS draft with Ryan Heath
summary: Jacob's 100-deep WR board moves **Matthew Golden to WR11** (four 12-target games, a league-high seven drops) and tells you to buy him. He keeps Watson a spot higher. He's nervous about Nabers and Jefferson because of McCarthy and Kyler, would **sell Garrett Wilson** (WR19) on name value, and likes **A.J. Brown** as a buy because his 16.7 XFP/g dwarfs his 6.75 PPG. Coker stays WR20 ("not moving Coker"). Concepcion is his top rookie, and Antonio Williams is a drop-Downs-for-him add. For Poncho: keep Coker in on Thursday, and treat Diggs as a top-20-type PPR WR only if his hand is OK. Jefferson (SUPERFLEX) may get outscored by Golden.

disagreements.Other side: Josh Norris: "I think Garrett Wilson's a buy" (SVF8). Adam Aizer agrees on the scary late schedule

disagreements.Jacob: Buy ("real chance… gets back on track")
disagreements.Other side: Hayden Winks: "the film is doing quite the opposite" (SVF8)

disagreements.Jacob: Top-20 weekly WR most weeks in PPR
disagreements.Other side: Hayden: "a part-time player"; Scott Turner relays Dan Quinn that Diggs's workload "isn't going to change"
Dave Richard: Burden over Coker in Wk8 and "can't resist starting Luther Burden"
Dave Richard and Scott Turner: the Lemon breakout is a 2027 thing

predictions.prediction: Golden outscores Justin Jefferson ROS.
Golden finishes as a top-12 WR ROS (ranked WR11).
A.J. Brown gets back on track (top-24 PPR WR PPG Wks 8-12).
Garrett Wilson is a sell (outside top-24 PPR WR PPG Wks 8-17).
Diggs is a top-20 weekly PPR WR in most of his games (Wks 8-12).
Burden outscores Odunze ROS.
Tee Higgins stays a top-15 WR ROS.
Antonio Williams outscores Josh Downs ROS.
Concepcion is the best rookie WR ROS (outscores Tate, Cooper and Boston).
Justin Jefferson finishes outside the top 12 ROS (ranked ~WR14; "nervous").

takeaways: Buy Golden before the drops stop; Jacob would pay a Nico/Nabers/Jefferson tier for "Golden plus."
Sell Garrett Wilson (and maybe Breece Hall) on name value before the late-season schedule.
Hold A.J. Brown or buy him cheap; the XFP says the points are coming.
Coker stays a WR2/3 for Jacob even after the 1.9-point dud.
Rookie order ROS: Concepcion > Tate > Cooper > Boston; Antonio Williams > Josh Downs.
Flournoy and Caleb Douglas are deep-roster keeps he likes.
my_notes:
Sleeper lineups pulled live ~9:12 PM ET Wed. ⚠️ Yahoo files are stale (Sun 10/25 5:58 PM ET).
- **Sleeper MAIN (Taylor Snift):** Coker (starting, WR20) is "the man," so keep him in on TNF. Diggs (starting, ~WR27) is a "top 20 weekly receiver most weeks" if healthy, but he's Questionable after a Wednesday DNP (hand). Caleb Douglas (bench) is Jacob's "love this guy" pivot. Worthy (~WR49) and Keon Coleman (~WR51) are bench-only. Chiefs offense "scares the crap out of" him (Worthy, Mahomes).
- **Sleeper DYNASTY (Amon A Boat!):** Amon-Ra is his WR3 ROS (Questionable, ankle, DNP Wed). Diggs and Douglas start. Odunze (bench) sits around WR37 in a downfield role he distrusts. Jacob would explore selling **Breece Hall** before his usage disappoints. Tank Dell "he's back, he's fine." Quentin Johnston and Brenen Thompson ("I love this guy") are deep stashes. Keenan Allen sits in the ~WR56-60 PPR-flex range.
- **Yahoo HE-MAN'S HEROES (The Cook King Show, stale):** Odunze ~WR37. McConkey moved up (concussion behind him; PIT trade rumors). Jordyn Tyson ~WR42, "absolutely" could climb if he plays. Shaheed not ranked aloud.
- **Yahoo SUPERFLEX (Jackson My Penix, stale):** Jefferson ~WR14, and Jacob thinks "there's a good chance Golden outscores him." DeVonta Smith WR22 ("very, very nervous"). Waddle ~WR30. Caleb Douglas and Flournoy (WR47) are both liked holds.
- **Freddy:** DYN starts McMillan (WR16), Jameson Williams (~WR23, "if you'd rather have Jameson Williams, that is probably valid") and Germie Bernard (WR44, sliding). MAIN starts Zay Flowers (top 8 but "I just don't know where we're at with the quarterback play") and Antonio Williams (rising).

Sleeper rosters pulled live from the public Sleeper API at ~6:25 PM ET on 10/28 (Week 8). Injury tags come from my 10/24 player cache plus today's other routines (Breece Questionable; Tyler Warren Questionable per the 9:45 AM check). ⚠️ **Yahoo files are stale** (`/workspace/myleague/yahoo/*.md`, fetched 10/25 for Week 7), so Yahoo roster context may have changed.

**Sleeper MAIN (Taylor Snift).** Starting RBs: Jonathan Taylor, Ollie Gordon II, Omarion Hampton (FLEX), Jordan Mason (FLEX); David Montgomery (Out) on the bench.
- Jacob still has **JT ~RB7** but flagged the Quenton Nelson trade and possible JT trade talk. Keep starting him; he's the guy you'd only move for an elite return.
- **Ollie Gordon RB19 ⬆** with RB1 XFP in Week 7: a confident start.
- **Mason (~RB26)** and **Hampton (~RB29)** are both FLEX-grade bets in his view, not locks. Sal Vetri said this morning to shop Mason; Jacob says hold, with upside if Jones misses time.
- **Montgomery (~RB34)** sits behind Woody Marks; Jacob is "pretty nervous" about his health. He's a drop candidate if you need the bench spot.

**Sleeper DYNASTY (Amon A Boat!).** Starting RBs: Kenneth Walker, Breece Hall (Questionable); bench Braelon Allen, Rico Dowdle (Questionable), Rachaad White, Justice Hill, Isiah Pacheco (IR).
- **Walker:** Jacob would "consider" selling him only for one of the absolute best players, citing KC's late schedule. In dynasty, a contender probably holds; it's worth listening to offers, though.
- **Breece (~RB22) vs. Braelon (mid-30s):** Jacob thinks the split Jets backfield is hard to trust either way. If Breece is ruled out, Braelon (20 XFP in Week 7) is the natural swap.
- **Dowdle** is a better stash than **Rachaad White** in his view (White RB43, "more than five points" doubt). Dowdle could be a top-12 RB if Warren went down.
- Jacob noted WAS "just lost Terry McLaurin." If that holds, more targets may flow to **Stefon Diggs**, who starts in both Sleeper leagues. That's my inference, not his call.

**Yahoo HE-MAN'S HEROES (The Cook King Show)** (stale 10/25 file): Henry, Swift, Ollie Gordon and Jacobs were in the lineup, with James Cook on the bench.
- **James Cook (~RB6) should not be benched** if he's active. On the 10/25 file he sat behind Jacobs (RB18) at W/R/T. Check this before Week 8 locks.
- **Henry RB5** depends on Lamar's return. **Swift ~RB12** (slight hit when Monangai returns). **Jacobs RB18**, with receiving upside after a 44% route rate.

**Yahoo SUPERFLEX (Jackson My Penix)** (stale 10/25 file): Judkins, Mason and Braelon Allen started, with Alvin Kamara on the bench.
- **Judkins moved up to RB20** and has a strong playoff schedule: keep starting him.
- **Mason (~RB26)** and **Braelon (mid-30s)** are FLEX-grade. Kamara wasn't ranked aloud.

summary: Nick Ercolano (sick, in a hoodie, no Monday stream) tiers every Week 8 RB. The headline calls are to stay on **Chase Brown** (75% snaps), ignore Pollard's and Judkins's spike weeks, make **Breece the workhorse over Braelon**, take **Coleman over Dobbins** but only as a shaky flex vs KC, and play **Rachaad White** as a high dub flex. **Jordan Mason** depends entirely on Aaron Jones's knee. For you, **DYN has Rachaad White on the bench while a Questionable Tyler Warren starts at FLEX**. MAIN's lineup is now full, and Hampton (shaky flex) is its weakest spot. Sleeper confirms most of Nick's numbers. He was off on Coleman's snaps (Sleeper has 30 vs 14, he said 28 vs 12), White's Week 6 snap share (69%, not 75-80%) and Jeanty's rank (RB10 total and RB12 PPG, not RB13). Yahoo data is still from 10/25.

disagreements.text: JT staying in Indy: Michael O'Hara (BDGE-6) said it's "more likely he stays." Nick doubts the front office report. They're mildly split inside BDGE.
Jonah Coleman: Nick is in line with O'Hara's No. 1 pickup on the long-term view, but he's colder for Week 8 (shaky flex vs KC).
Jordan Mason: Sal Vetri (today) says to shop Mason. Nick says it's "so not clear," which fits a shop-or-hold call over a buy.
Braelon Allen: Nick sees no 50/50 split once Breece is back, against the crowd he's arguing with.

predictions.prediction: Pollard gets "pretty much a guaranteed 18 touches" if Spears sits.
Chase Brown's TD luck turns. Grade (mine): a Brown TD in Wk8 vs TEN.
Breece plays Wk8 with about a 65-70% share; Braelon gets around 30%.
Jordan Mason gets 15-18+ carries if Aaron Jones sits.
JT gets 70%+ of the IND RB touches in Wk8 (no trade).
Jonah Coleman out-snaps Dobbins again in Wk8.
Ollie Gordon's floor is "very very very high." Grade: 12+ PPR in Wk8.
Rachaad White is a high dub flex. Grade: RB24-or-better PPR in Wk8.
Monangai is 50/50 to play MNF.
If Charbonnet plays, it's a split; nobody in that backfield is startable.
Bucky Irving is "a pretty solid RB1." Grade: RB12-or-better in Wk8.
Henry needs Lamar; Henry gets 82.5+ rushing yards if Lamar plays.

takeaways: Rachaad White is a high dub flex with Croskey-Merritt on IR. (He's on your DYN bench; see below.)
Jordan Mason's value depends on Aaron Jones's Wednesday and Thursday practices. He's a dub flex if Jones sits and a shaky flex if Jones plays. Check the Friday report before locking a FLEX.
Breece over Braelon if Breece gets a full practice. Braelon is now Questionable (ankle) in Sleeper too.
Ollie Gordon is Feels Good, with TDs in four straight games and Wright Questionable.
Stay on Chase Brown (75% snaps) and don't chase the Pollard or Judkins spike weeks.
Coleman over Dobbins rest of season, but both Denver RBs are only shaky flexes vs KC.
Lamar is trending toward playing, but keep a backup QB.
Saquon is a hampered Feels Good; Elijah Mitchell is the free speculative add.
Don't start Charbonnet in his first game back, and fade Monangai in his first.

title: Sal Vetri: "5 Players About to GO NUCLEAR in Fantasy (Trade For Them Now)" — actually his Week 7 → 8 panic meter
summary: Sal's Tuesday video (17:28, solo) carries a recycled "GO NUCLEAR" title, but it's really his panic meter on seven players. He's calm on most of them: **A.J. Brown** (very little panic, buy low: 94% routes and 27% share while still recovering from the high-ankle sprain), **Jalen Coker** (1/10, blowout noise, better than McMillan), **Nico Collins** (1/10, don't sell low through the bye), **Olave** (3/10, Shough's broken hand), **Garrett Wilson** (4/10, target competition from Cooper, Mitchell, Mason Taylor and Breece), and **Chase Brown** (4/10, fumbles and the JT-to-CIN rumor). The one real alarm is **Denzel Boston** (6–7/10), as **KC Concepcion** breaks out. He also softened on a JT trade compared with yesterday. For you: start **Coker** Thursday in MAIN, hold **JT**, and look at **Mason Taylor** (FA in MAIN). Watch **Breece Hall's** Wk8 return in DYNASTY, where Freddy's Fannin is the one Sal likes. title: Week 8 Waiver Wire: MUST ADD Players, Injury Replacements & Streamers | 2026 Fantasy Football Advice
summary:
Adam, Jamey and Dave spent 67 minutes on the Week 8 wire and couldn't agree on a clean top three. Jamey leads with **Seth McGowan** (a Jonathan Taylor trade bet), **KC Concepcion**, and **Hunter Henry**. **Henry** is everyone's TE: four straight 11+ games, and MIA has allowed 9.2+ to TEs every week. On other sites, **Omar Cooper Jr.**, **Rachaad White** and **Jonah Coleman** are must-adds. The QB streams are **Cousins > Brissett ≈ Geno**, with **Malik Willis** as the bye-week stash, and the **Jaguars DST** and **Cam Little** lead the streamers.

The big fight was over **Makai Lemon**. Adam and Jamey call him a must-add with DeVonta Smith out, while Dave won't "expect big things." Sleeper's data favors the bulls: 91% of snaps and 6+ targets four weeks running. On FAB, the message was "not an empty-the-bank week."

Almost every stat checked against Sleeper held up. The exceptions are Antonio Williams's "8 targets without Diggs" (Diggs played that game), CMC's injury (calf in Sleeper, not hamstring), and two small scoring-dependent slips.

For you, Poncho, the show backs the morning plan in all four leagues:
- **MAIN:** Little, Lemon and Keaton Mitchell; drop Kendre.
- **DYNASTY:** Mason Taylor. Freddy's Goff draws the Vikings.
- **HEROES:** Henry, then Lemon.
- **SUPERFLEX:** Activate Lamar and add Lemon.

takeaways: If they're free (mostly Yahoo): Omar Cooper Jr. > Rachaad White / Jonah Coleman ("must add across the board"). Cooper is the one worth a real bid. Take White for a Wk8 RB need, Coleman for the long term.

WR: Concepcion > Caleb Douglas > Makai Lemon ≥ Antonio Williams. Lemon is the swing guy: Adam and Jamey say must-add (DeVonta out, WAS secondary), while Dave says don't expect much. In MAIN, ~$14 (this morning's plan) is fine.
TE: Hunter Henry (consensus #1), then Hockenson (this week, @DET) or Okonkwo (ROS). Mason Taylor (LV has allowed 8 TE TDs) is the cheap option that almost nobody rosters.
QB streams: Cousins (if he was dropped) > Brissett ≈ Geno > Rodgers; Penix only in SF/2QB. Stash Malik Willis for Wks 9–11.

RB: Stash Kaelon Black (CMC) and McGowan (JT trade). For a Wk8 body: Emanuel Wilson (if Charbonnet/Price sit) > Sampson > Perine. Elijah Mitchell only if Saquon and Pierce are both out; Knight only if Love sits.
DST/K: Jaguars (vs IND) > Bengals > Bears; Cam Little > Boswell > Gay.
Drops: Juwan Johnson, Kendre Miller, Devaughn Vele and Tyler Shough (byes), Tank Dell, Malik Washington, Wan'Dale Robinson, Allgeier. Hold Sutton (Waddle insurance) and Denzel Boston.
Saturday stashes (claims 3–4): Tyrone Tracy, Devin Singletary, Deebo (if somehow free), Jordyn Tyson.

title: Beyond the Box Score report — Week 7 Recap: "Who Should You Be Worried About? Collins, Henry, Chase Brown, & More!"
summary: The Week 7 Recap was a "don't panic" episode. Henry is the least worrying of the four flagged players (it's a Lamar problem). Nico and Garrett Wilson are real but moderate worries, and Wilson's playoff schedule is ugly. Chase Brown's usage (75.5% snaps) is fine minus the goal-line TD. Zay Flowers is the consensus "next JSN," and his Lamar split is absurd. Tate is the rookie with true WR2 usage; Cooper Jr. and Concepcion are YAC darlings with role/TD questions. For Poncho, the action items are: start Allen over Mahomes in MAIN and fade Worthy @ DEN; hold Henry; Shaheed is Out; watch Waddle's arm in SUPERFLEX; keep Pitts rolling; and consider Mason Taylor and Caleb Douglas.

takeaways: Start Zay Flowers every week, and more so once Lamar is back (7.8 YPRR in 45 routes with Lamar). The whole panel agrees.
Hold Derrick Henry. It's "purely a Lamar issue," and last year's slow start turned into a monster finish.
KC is a fade at @ DEN in Week 8. Dan doesn't trust Mahomes, Worthy, or anyone but Walker. Kelce is only a matchup play.
Lions vs MIN is a Goff-downgrade spot (Flores blitzed ~88% Sunday). Temper Jameson Williams and LaPorta.

Rookie WR stash order from the panel: Tate (usage) > Cooper Jr. (talent/YAC, opportunity risk) ≈ Concepcion (YAC, no TD looks) > Boston (boom/bust). Sleepers: Antonio Williams, Malachi Fields, Caleb Douglas (and Tyson when healthy).
Mason Taylor deserves a look. Dan's film says he was wide open for what "should have been a three touchdown game." (He's on the MAIN and DYN wires per the Oct 27 Sleeper pull.)
Pitts: 20%+ TPRR four straight games plus 4 TD in 3 games. Keep starting him.
Garrett Wilson sellers' window: his last 5 fantasy weeks (bye, Surtain, ARI, Gonzalez, MIN) are ugly.
Raiders QB risk: Kubiak wouldn't commit to Cousins. That's a risk for Tucker, and Dan thinks Bowers gets more first-read looks with Mendoza.
Darnold is a Week 8 streamer vs CHI per Adam (free in MAIN).

- **Jordan Mason** (MIN): Aaron Jones' knee is "not serious," per Adam, so Mason's share may shrink when Jones returns.

- **Mark Andrews** (bench): Lamar's return should help BAL pass-catchers (see Flowers' Lamar split).
- **Waivers:** Makai Lemon was mentioned only as the MNF wild card. The Wk 8 waiver memo already has him at $14. Mason Taylor is free per the Oct 27 pull (Dan's open-TE film). Darnold is free if you want a QB2.

**Sleeper DYNASTY, Amon A Boat!**
- **Kenneth Walker III (KC):** "nothing wrong with Kenneth Walker." Keep starting him.
- **Rashid Shaheed (SEA):** knee injury, extent unknown on the show. Sleeper now lists him **Out**, so swap him out.
- **Brock Bowers (LV):** Dan thinks a Mendoza switch funnels first reads to Bowers, but the pass volume could drop. Jeanty's 83-catch pace also cuts into the pie.
- **Amon-Ra St. Brown (DET vs MIN):** a Goff downgrade spot. Still start him; he's a stud.
- **T.J. Hockenson (MIN):** no mention.
- **Caleb Douglas** (bench): same bullish read as above; a dynasty hold.
- **Jayden Daniels / Rachaad White (WAS):** Dan says Daniels "looks pretty good throwing the ball," and Antonio Williams is a sleeper with McLaurin out for the year. (Antonio Williams is on Freddy's MAIN roster, not available.)
- **Mason Taylor:** free in DYN per the pull and already the waiver memo's top DYN add. The show's film reinforces it.

- **Derrick Henry:** hold and start. The panel is unanimous that he's the least concerning.
- **Mahomes:** same fade @ DEN. Consider Mayfield if he's still rostered (the waiver memo suggested dropping him).
- **D'Andre Swift / Rome Odunze (CHI @ SEA MNF):** Jacob is "confident" in Swift generally. Dan and Jacob say the Bears are unpredictable, and SEA's defense was a "buzzsaw." Odunze wasn't discussed. Note that SEA's LT Cross is out, which helps CHI's pass rush, not their offense.

- **Rashid Shaheed:** knee injury (Sleeper: Out).

- **Jaylen Waddle (DEN):** arm injury, "could be major." He's a starter here, so monitor it and line up a backup.
- **Kyle Pitts:** Adam is bullish (20%+ TPRR four straight games, 4 TD in 3 games). Keep starting him.

- **Braelon Allen (NYJ):** no direct take. Dan's Geno film shows a QB missing open players, which is a mild offense concern.

- **Mark Andrews:** Lamar's return helps.

title: 🏈 BDGE BREAKDOWN: "Rookies Are Blasting Off Everywhere" (Week 8 Waiver Wire)
summary: Michael O'Hara's Week 8 waiver show crowns **Jonah Coleman** the No. 1 pickup (15–18%+ FAAB), with Brissett as the top QB streamer and Geno right behind. He calls **Lemon** and **Okonkwo** must-adds, and both are free in your MAIN. He likes **Flournoy** as a three-week flex (keep him in SUPERFLEX) and tells you to cut **Keon Coleman**, which is on your MAIN bench. JT is "more likely" to stay in Indy. Sleeper also shows an **empty starter and Mahomes over Allen in MAIN**, plus **Rodgers and an Out Shaheed starting in DYN**. Stats checked against Sleeper all match except two small misses: Okonkwo had 69 yards, not 76, and Sampson's snap share was 46%, not 47%. Yahoo data is still from 10/25.

Jonah Coleman's role grows, and he could "just ice" Dobbins.

takeaways: Jonah Coleman is the add of the week if he's free anywhere (he's rostered in both Sleeper leagues).
Makai Lemon for WR depth with DeVonta still out. He's free in your MAIN.
Chig Okonkwo is O'Hara's top TE add. He's free in your MAIN.
QB streams: Brissett vs DAL > Geno vs LV > Penix / Mayfield. McCarthy is a superflex hold (NYG bye).
Keep Flournoy as a 3-week flex (ARI, IND, SF).
Cheap RB lottery: Elijah Mitchell $1–2; Bam Knight a couple bucks only if Love looks iffy. Don't spend real FAAB.

Cuts: Keon Coleman, Kendre Miller, Jake Ferguson, Sadiq, Mumpfield, Lloyd, Darius Cooper, Cooks / Kirk, and Addison in shallow leagues.

title: Sal Vetri: "10 Must Add Players to Pick Up in Your Fantasy League Right Now" (Week 8 waivers)
summary: Sal's Week 8 waiver video (18:24, solo) is rookie-heavy. The headline adds are **Omar Cooper Jr.** ("number one ad by far," back-to-back 100-yard TD games), **Jonah Coleman** (50% snaps in his IR return, and sell RJ Harvey high), **Makai Lemon** (DeVonta Smith IR or shutdown risk), plus the TEs **Brenton Strange** and **Chig Okonkwo**. His stashes are **Jordyn Tyson** (15+ PPG playoff ceiling), **Seth McGowan** (he now leans that IND trades JT), Antonio Williams, Singletary, Pat Bryant, Travis Hunter (deep only), and handcuffs Kaelon Black and Emmett Johnson. He flipped on Coleman (RB50 noise on Sunday), on Cooper and on a JT trade. For you: keep Tyson on HEROES IR, watch **Waddle's shoulder** and move on from **DeVonta Smith** in SUPERFLEX (Lemon is the swap if free), hold JT and Diggs in MAIN, and consider Lemon or Singletary as MAIN FAs. In DYNASTY, Freddy owns **Emmett Johnson**, the handcuff for your Kenneth Walker III.

title: EARLY Week 8 Waiver Wire TARGETS! McGowan, Douglas, Concepcion, Williams, & Others! (FFT Express)

summary: A quick Monday Express: Jamey's early Week 8 list leads with Seth McGowan (a Jonathan Taylor trade bet), Zonovan Knight (the one RB who can start now), the rookie WRs Concepcion and Douglas, and Antonio Williams. takeaways: Omar Cooper Jr. was the show's consensus darling and delivered (WR4, 5-115-1). Harmon's "better than anything Adonai Mitchell's done" film take looks right; he beat Keenan Allen, Malik Washington and KC in every question he was in.
Josh's best calls of the day were the quiet ones: Caleb Douglas over Ted Hurst (20.0 vs 0.0), Cooper over Keenan, Tee Higgins "about to go crazy" (WR1), and Tony Pollard "welcome to" (RB1, 3 TD).
The flag plants mostly flopped: Woody Marks (RB24, HOU lost in OT) and Denzel Boston (3-27) missed; Kraft is the one still alive.
Jordan Mason was the most-mentioned player and a dud (6.8, no catches). The "drive-by-drive" split read was right; the "big second half" read wasn't, because MIN never blew IND out (16-10).
Hayden's "attack cluster injuries" model: Bucky vs CAR's missing corners hit (RB2). The LAR-defense angle (Mayer, Jeanty) and the GB-LB angle (Goff/Gibbs) are not paying yet.
The fade-the-NYG-backfield call (Boone) missed badly: Skattebo 124 yards and a TD (RB6).
Higbee top-7 TE (Hayden) is at 0.4 with LAR up 28-6, a blowout that's killing LAR pass volume.
Things still to settle tonight and Monday: Emanuel Wilson (Josh vs Boone), Saquon RB7-9, Lemon, Pickens, Kelce "six catches", Goedert TE4.

title: Sal Vetri: "Answering Your Week 7 Fantasy Football Questions Right Now" (Sunday morning live Q&A)
summary: Sal's Sunday-morning Super Chat stream is a 46-minute rapid-fire start/sit session. Its loudest takes: start Puka if active (✅ 17.8), Braelon over Woody Marks with Breece out (✅), buy Josh Jacobs (✅ 17.6), Ollie Gordon is "the ultimate sell high," trade DeVonta Smith ASAP, Jonah Coleman is RB50 noise, JT probably isn't traded, and he's skipping next Sunday's stream for the NYC Marathon. On decided Wk7 calls he went about 20-13-1 (≈60%). Big hits were Pollard, Jameson Williams, Nix and Judkins; big misses were Higbee over Hockenson, Bryce over Stafford, Aaron Jones and Wan'Dale over Concepcion. For you: hold Hockenson, Caleb Douglas and Pitts despite Sal's lukewarm takes, consider shopping Ollie Gordon (MAIN/HEROES), and treat DeVonta Smith (SUPERFLEX) as a sell/IR risk.

segments.title: Open at halftime of NO-PIT (13-10), "Jaylen Warren going off once again." News: Breece Hall unlikely (Rapoport), 4th straight miss. Puka Nacua: "optimistic he will play"; "if he suits up, you play Puka… one quarter of Puka is going to be better than the entire game of KaVontae Turpin." Have a late-window replacement ready. NYG backfield: "Cam Akers"❓ RB1 usage report vs. conflicting 50-50 report; Sal expects a split because NYG are 9.5-pt dogs vs HOU, so Tyrone Tracy's passing-down role.
Stakes rant: Wk7 swing week; 3-3 swing, 2-4 do-or-die, 1-5/0-6 "probably already cooked."
Q&A begins. Darius Cooper over Pitts/Corum (Corum in standard). DeVonta Smith re-aggravated hamstring a 3rd time, "IR stint on the way?" concern.

"Culker"❓ over E. Wilson / Jonah Coleman: "different stratosphere." Boston over Bam Knight (Knight's prop ~9.5 carries, no passing-down role; Boston ~20% target share). Omar Cooper over Caleb Douglas (Douglas back from high-ankle; Willis has a Malik Washington connection; Adonai Mitchell + Quentin Johnston healthy).

Golden over Woody Marks (both 16+ PPR projected; GB dogs vs DET, who allow the most passing yards/game; "YOLO ball"). Higbee over Hockenson and Kmet (MIN weapons back, Jefferson fully healthy; Higbee #1 option if Puka misses). Hardman flex. Bryce Young over Stafford (Adams hurt, Puka timing).

E. Wilson over Higbee/Mason (~a dozen carries + red-zone role). Braelon over Woody Marks if Breece out. Keep Kirk Cousins; Saquon over Braelon (Braelon = RB14; Saquon prop ~16 carries, ~20 opportunities).

Aaron Jones over Josh Downs/Allgeier/Knight: Jones/Mason 10-12 carries each, checkdowns to Jones with Kyler Murray; "minor MCL" theory. Fant over Pitts. Sal's own Sat-morning players: DK Metcalf (Flock), Germie Bernard.

"Crazy to start Kyler over JT? Yes, extremely crazy." 5-man lineup Q: start JT, Watson, sit Pickens (DAL), Braelon over Woody Marks. Godwin over Mason/Malik Washington ("Mason… the most touchdown-or-bust player maybe in the NFL"; "<7 fantasy points a game" with Jones active). Skattebo over AD Mitchell; Hardman over Rondale Moore; Goff over Purdy.
Trade Q: keep Pickens over Rashee Rice + Egbuka (two injured players; Rice hasn't practiced, hamstring on top of knee; Egbuka concussion + foot/toe). Judkins over Tate.
Jonah Coleman rant: "I don't really get the hype"; Sean Payton calling plays, Dobbins 60%+ snaps, Justice Hill❓ pass-down back; Coleman = "my running back 50," ~4 points. Skattebo over Justice Hill.
Garbled 16-team flurry (see name table; low trust). Titans DEF pickup over Rams/Bengals: "a top-five defense this week."
Vele vs Addison: hold Vele; Addison has re-injured that hamstring ~3 times since college; Week 9 return not guaranteed. "Addison is levels better… but that's a big if."
Wan'Dale Robinson over KC Concepcion ("kind of have a feeling this is a Concepcion breakout" but Jeudy squeezing Concepcion's routes; Jeudy not getting traded, CLE 4-2). Tre Tucker flex.

Puka timing: decision at ~2:55 PM ET. Drop Mumpfield, add Makai Lemon; "if Puka's in, start Puka, if he's out, start Lemon." Saquon #1, Braelon over Marks. Keenan/Braelon. Bryce over Purdy; Woody Marks over Pickens; RJ Harvey over Bam/Allgeier; Higbee over Hock again.
Buy Josh Jacobs with Jeremiyah Love: "borderline top 30 player rest of season… if we redrafted today, he's a third-round pick."
Half-PPR manifesto: "half PPR rankings are the only rankings that matter," ~98-99% overlap. Concepcion over Mason; Goedert over Hock; Worthy #1 + Harvey.

Jameson Williams over E. Wilson/Rondale (DET off bye, 32.5 implied team total, highest of the week, shootout vs GB). Michael Wilson over Waddle. Pollard flex (NYG allowing 27+ to all but TEN; MIN allow 12.8 ppg❓ context unclear). JT over Marks.

Long bench-crunch answer: don't drop Jacobs/Tuten; "DJ Moore and Michael Wilson are top 50 players rest of season"; with a winning record, consider not starting a QB or TE; drop Higbee, stream Penix, maybe Jake Ferguson on MNF. Makai Lemon over Mason; Keenan Allen over Darius Cooper/MHJ/Parkinson.

Game back on: Vele 5-54-1. Sal glad "Zofa" dropped Vele in the Flock League. Mumpfield vs Flournoy: "probably neither," Flournoy. Jacobs + Waddle over Gordon/Boston. Nico over Woody Marks. Aaron Jones over Mason.
Waddle sell-high plan: best matchup of the year vs ARI ("Cardinals allow the most passing yards per play"); if he pops, sell, and "do not trick yourself into thinking Bo Nix is back."
Inactives: Tyjae Spears inactive (Pollard upgrade), Breece Hall officially out, Braelon "nearly… top 12 running back." DJ Moore over Latavius❓/Germie Bernard ROS. Taysom Hill red-zone INT.
Don't drop Sutton for J.J. McCarthy in 1QB.

Olave for Burden + Ollie Gordon + Tank Dell = "you got fleeced." Olave top-15 ROS; Burden "barely in the top like 40"; Gordon "the ultimate sell high"; Tank Dell "nothing" ("their own coaching staff… hoping to get something out of Tank Dell in 2027").
5-1 manager: start Dak + CeeDee over Stafford.
Goedert over Kelce (National Tight Ends Day primetime joke: "pan to Taylor Swift seven times"); Goedert = only viable target for Tanner McKee.
"Skowronek"❓ over Mumpfield/Cooper; Rodgers' dropped-ball moment ("laughing at the old man"); Judkins & Higbee over MHJ; "Rico Dowdle is just buns." Waddle + Downs; Mims❓ ~10 projected.
Jacobs over M. Wilson; Hockenson over "Harold Landry"❓; Bucky over Dobbins.

Rice for Vele + Aaron Jones: prefer the Rice side, "nothing burger"; Vele and Jones = sell-highs, Rice "decent buy low" with hamstring worry. London + Lamb over Nabers/Watson. Golden + Hubbard over Warren + Higgins ("much rather have Golden over Higgins rest of season").
DeVonta Smith: "I'd try and trade him as soon as possible." Sirianni didn't rule out shutting him down; best bet misses ≥1 more game with an IR chance; no Jalen Hurts the rest of the year.

Superflex drops: Downs and "I Don't Say"❓ over Charbonnet. Keenan Allen over Boston. Jacobs/Price/Tate/Bernard vs Chase Brown/McConkey/Kamara/Harvey: take Jacobs side; Price "means nothing." Saquon over "Coker"❓.

JT trade talk: >50% he's not traded; Colts would want a 1st or early 2nd for "an aging running back"; if traded, McGowan probably not a workhorse (split or an RB comes back, e.g. Charbonnet as a hypothetical).
Horrible RB2 options: Samaje Perine; Kelce over Higbee. Downs over Malik Washington/Lemon. Schultz/Mayer, then Otton is "my tight end 10."

Trades: keep Young/Barkley/Golden over Love/Mason/Brock; Javonte/Tate/Stevenson for Breece + Zay Flowers good if they were depth. Gordon flex. Bourne over Noel; Ja'Kobi Lane now a fade (Bateman practiced full). Cousins vs Nix: flips to Nix. Worthy over Godwin. Drop Mayer for Otton.
1-5 manager: drop Godwin for Lemon (Lemon better ROS; Godwin = WR30 this week, Lemon WR33). Non-PPR: Nico + Marks.

Sign-off: Wk7-9 most pivotal; usual schedule (Mon waivers, Tue panics, daily videos Mon-Sat). Not live next Sunday: running the New York City Marathon; live Mon night (10/26) and Thursday, then probably not until the following Thursday.

mode: Fast-twitch Super Chat triage with the NO-PIT game on screen. Confident, decisive, a little punchy ("you got fleeced," "Rico Dowdle is just buns," "the absolute biggest of dunces"). Personal stakes on display (DK Metcalf, Germie Bernard, the Flock League).
notes: Puka plays → start him, period (5). ✅
Braelon Allen locked in with Breece out (5). ✅
Jonah Coleman is irrelevant while Dobbins is healthy (5).
Josh Jacobs is a buy, borderline top-30 ROS (4). Strong Wk7 return.
Ollie Gordon is "the ultimate sell high" (4). Gordon still scored 16.8.
JT stays in Indy (>50%) (3).
Higbee as Rams' #1 target if Puka out (3). Puka played and Higbee busted.
Bryce Young over Stafford (3). Bust.

title: Week 7 Winners & Losers: Biggest Takeaways From Every Game! | 2026 Fantasy Football Advice
summary: Week 7's Winners & Losers belonged to the runners: Pollard (36.5 PPR), Bucky (Heath: top-12 RB), Judkins (Dave: locked-in RB2) and a Skattebo comeback, while Nico Collins (2.6) and Garrett Wilson (4.6) got demoted to WR2/sell-after-a-good-game. Jamey's rookies Concepcion and Cooper Jr. are now WR3 starts, the Vikings' passing game was trashed (Jefferson "high-end WR2," Mason a "trap back"), LaPorta flopped but stays a start, and Adam got roasted for doubting Bijan and talking up Godwin. For you: keep starting Ollie Gordon, bench Kendre Miller and Kamara (NO bye) and find a kicker for Fairbairn (HOU bye) and a TE for Kittle (SF bye), consider Caleb Douglas over Coker, look at Malik Willis over Rodgers in DYNASTY, and watch Waddle's shoulder and Aaron Jones's knee.

summary: Sunday-morning lightning round with Adam, Dave and Heath before the 9:30 AM ET kickoff. The big news was Jacobs getting a "normal allotment" (Heath ~RB17), Puka expected but not certain, Skattebo back as the Giants' lead back with Tracy mixing in (avoid both), and Breece unlikely (now Out, so Braelon Allen is an RB2). Every stat I could check against Sleeper held up except Tre Tucker's "never stacks" numbers, which don't include his 2026 Week 2-3 follow-up (8.3 PPR).

title: LAST-MINUTE Week 7 Fantasy Football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Advice! Actives/Inactives & Q&A (FFT Express)
summary: Adam and Heath ran a 9-minute pre-show at about 8 AM. The calls that hit were Braelon over the field with Breece out, Judkins as a top-20 back, Willis over Daniel Jones, Pollard over Corum, and Bam Knight over Allgeier. The misses were the Vikings backfield (Jones 3.6, Mason 6.8), Malik Washington's "11 points" (6.5), fading Omar Cooper (22.5), sitting Flowers for Chuba, and Tate over Kraft. For you, Braelon and Judkins delivered in Dynasty and SUPERFLEX, and Jacobs did in HEROES. Caleb Douglas (21.0) and Malik Willis (26.02) both sat on your benches.

disagreements.Result: Mason 6.8, Jones 3.6. MIN won 16-10, so the matchup take missed

disagreements.Heath: Expected to play; roster Mumpfield to wait him out

predictions.prediction: Malik Washington scores about 11 (Heath). ❌ 6.5
Bam Knight leads ARI in rush attempts (Heath). ❌ Allgeier had 8, Knight 7 (Knight did outscore him)
Daniel Jones is the lowest-projected QB (Heath). ✅ 4.62
Braelon over Jacobs (Heath). ❌ by 0.7
Start Carnell Tate over Kraft and Waddle (Heath). ❌
The Vikings backfield smashes the Colts (Adam). ❌

takeaways: Heath's projections are low on Jacobs, and he's been wrong twice. Jacobs scored 20.1 on 11 carries because of his 5 catches. Don't bench Jacobs for Braelon-tier backs off this show.
Braelon Allen is a real RB2 while Breece is out (19.4, 17 carries, 7 targets). He's the waiver or trade story for Week 8.
Caleb Douglas (21.0) and Tre Tucker (21.3) beat every WR on Heath's waiver list. Douglas is the add to make in leagues where he's still free.
Daniel Jones is unplayable (4.62; Heath has him as the lowest-projected QB). Malik Willis (26.02) is startable while he's the Miami QB.
The Vikings backfield is a split that should be faded. Mason had 15 carries for 68 yards and Jones 8 for 26, against a matchup Adam called great.
MNF hedges: Saquon is still Questionable, so Pierce owners should be ready. Goedert is a top-10 TE with Wicks and DeVonta Smith out. Flournoy, Lemon and Darius Cooper are late-swap options.
my_notes:
**Sleeper MAIN, Taylor Snift (you):**
- **Jordan Mason (started):** Heath had him third in his Minnesota group and Adam liked the matchup. He scored 6.8 PPR here (11.30 in your scoring) with no TD.
- **Kendre Miller (started):** lost to Bam Knight, Emanuel Wilson and Mason in the chat picks. The hosts were right to be cool on him (5.8).
- **Sam LaPorta (started):** Heath's pick over Goedert and Higbee. 1 catch on 2 targets. ❌
- **Caleb Douglas (bench):** Heath's "little bit of interest" guy scored 21.0. He's the bench lesson of the week. Start him next week if Willis keeps the job.
- **Freddy (Flowers for Ms. Jackson):** Heath told a viewer to sit **Zay Flowers** for Chuba; Flowers scored 27.7. **Saquon** is expected to play MNF; Freddy has **Dameon Pierce** as the exact handcuff. **Kelce** was Heath's pick over Higbee and has 0 so far on SNF. **Rico Dowdle** (bench) was confirmed active and scored 14.6.

**Sleeper DYNASTY, Amon A Boat! (you):**
- **Braelon Allen (started):** the show's top call for you. 19.4 ✅
- **Malik Willis (bench):** Heath's pick over Daniel Jones, and he scored 26.02 on your bench while Rodgers started (13.08). Willis deserves the QB spot while he's the Miami starter.
- **Breece Hall (Out):** Heath and Adam both said start Braelon; Breece's return will make it a split. That's a reason to hold, not sell, if the price is low.
- **Freddy (The Man in Jahmyr):** **Konata Mumpfield** started as the Puka hedge, but Puka played and Mumpfield scored 2.5. **Blake Corum** (bench) lost the Pollard pick and still scored 17.1. **Kendrick Bourne** was a named late option and scored 3.9. **Dylan Sampson** came off IR (10.7). **Jordan Addison** isn't helped by Minnesota's backfield split.

**Yahoo HE-MAN'S HEROES, The Cook King Show (you):**
- **Josh Jacobs (started at W/R/T):** Heath was "the low guy on Jacobs," but he scored 20.1 PPR on Sleeper. Good start.
- **Opponent Dirty Bois:** had **Braelon Allen** (Yahoo 24.65 at 5:58) and **Tyler Allgeier** (Heath preferred Knight; Allgeier scored 7.9). They also have Germie Bernard on the bench.

**Yahoo SUPERFLEX, Jackson My Penix (you):**
- **Quinshon Judkins (started):** Heath's "top 20-ish" back went off for 2 TDs (27.65 Yahoo). ✅
- **Braelon Allen (started at W/R/T):** 24.65 Yahoo. ✅
- **Jordan Mason (started):** 10.55 Yahoo. Fine, not great.
- **Jaylen Waddle (started):** lost Heath's three-way pick to Tate, then left with a chest injury (~8.8). Watch his practice reports this week.
- **Caleb Douglas (bench, 21.0)** and **Ryan Flournoy (bench, MNF; Adam's "five targets a game" fallback).**
- **Opponent 4th & Short Alexander:** Pat Freiermuth (Heath picked him over Parkinson; he scored 4.0), Aaron Jones (Heath's top Minnesota back; 3.6 PPR, Yahoo 5.6 at 5:58), and Godwin on the bench (6.7).

title: Sal Vetri: "This News Changes Everything (Week 7)"
summary: Sal's Friday-evening injury roundup gets most of the big calls right on paper: Lamar, DeVonta and Wicks are all Out per Sleeper, Woody Marks is a must-start, and Saquon is a top-12 back against DAL's leaky run defense. Breece Hall is now Out, so Braelon Allen moves into Sal's RB14 scenario, and he's already in your Amon A Boat! lineup. In Taylor Snift, Worthy is a confident start, Mason is touchdown-or-bust, and Kendre Miller is already locked in Paris. Freddy's Saquon, Zay Flowers and Kelce all get good news here. Puka is still a game-time call for the late games.

Saquon expected to play. PHI WR injuries (DeVonta, Wicks, Goedert knee), DAL run D allows most rush yds/g (149.8). Saquon 16 proj, top-12
Rashee Rice out again. Last week Worthy 27% TS, 7/7; Kelce 19% TS. Worthy WR26 (12.5), Kelce TE7 (11.7)
Montgomery out (groin), Jawhar Jordan IR → Woody Marks show (78% snaps, 61% rush att, 61% routes last week); ~16 proj, must start
DraftKings ad read

Zay Flowers without Lamar: 33% TS last two games, leads NFL in yards per route run; still top-15
Judkins returns, Dylan Sampson activated off IR. Judkins RB21, 12.2 proj, TD-dependent

title: Sal Vetri: "My Week 7 Running Backs Rankings and Tiers"
summary: Sal's Thursday RB tiers (released Fri 10/23) put Gibbs, CMC, Bijan and Kenneth Walker in the S tier and Hubbard in the A tier on elite usage. He calls Woody Marks a must-start with Montgomery out, says Braelon Allen is RB12 because he expects Breece Hall to sit, wants Jacobs back in lineups right away, and keeps hammering the Jeanty sell. For you, Poncho, the key decision is in dynasty: if Breece is inactive, start Braelon. In MAIN, Taylor, Gordon and Mason are fine, and Kendre Miller is a desperation flex, but byes leave you few better options.

segments.title: Intro, "new format" tiers. S tier (RB1-4): Gibbs, CMC, Bijan, Walker; Walker's SNF revenge spot vs SEA, KC team total 20
A tier (RB5-7): Kyren, Henry (Lamar ankle), Hubbard deep dive (87% snaps, 86% carries, 64% routes, >20 opps/g)
B tier part 1 (RB8-10): Taylor @ MIN (off bye), Javonte @ PHI MNF, Warren deep dive with Dowdle split and halftime numbers
B tier part 2 (RB11-13): Aaron Jones 16.4, Braelon 16.1 (efficiency praise, Breece quad), Bucky concern (PFF CAR run D 30th overall, interior DL top half; Baker; Sean Tucker practicing; illness)
B tier part 3 (RB14-17): Saquon returning (15.9, hamstring, McKee), Woody Marks (HOU -9.5, 26.5 total, Jawhar IR, 78/22 snaps), Montgomery DNP Thursday, Chase Brown, Jeanty "sell" rant
⚠️ Transcript gap (likely ad/membership read)

C tier (RB18-24): Pollard, Jacobs (over 11.5 carries bet), Judkins, Ollie Gordon, Denver duo (Payton play-calling, Harvey checkdowns "PPR cheat code… a scam"), Allgeier with Love out vs Bam Knight split

D tier (RB25-33): Wilson/Miller/Kamara/Corum/Knight/Charbonnet; Saints split, Etienne after Wk9 bye; Charbonnet vs Jacobs return contrast; Kyren complaint + "squeaky wheel"; Perine, Skattebo (Najee cut), Mason (Jones MCL)
Blueprint plug (start/sit tool, WR ranks to WR105, trade calc, ~8,000 members)
E tier (RB34-41/42): Dowdle, Gainwell, Mike Washington Jr., Spears (drop), Tracy (stash), B-Rob, Justice Hill, Holani
F tier (RB43-50): stash names (Kaelon Black, Emmett Johnson, Vaki), Jawhar Jordan officially on IR mid-recording, Gibbs handcuff talk, Pacheco
Outro; asks for feedback on tier format

tone: Brisk, workmanlike, more of a lineup-setting tool than a hot-take show. Mildly self-deprecating about the new format ("a little bit wonky… just bear with me"). The most emotional moment is the Jeanty section, which is close to exasperated.
kyren squeaky-wheel bump: 2 ("I don't know if we do get that")
mason rise: 3, conditional on a full Friday practice
bullish: Hubbard, Woody Marks, Braelon Allen, Josh Jacobs, Ollie Gordon (grudgingly), Jordan Mason (conditional), Tyrone Tracy (stash), Mike Washington Jr. (stash), Kendre Miller over Kamara.
bearish: Jeanty, RJ Harvey, Bucky Irving (this week), Zach Charbonnet, Blake Corum, Tyjae Spears, all D-tier RBs vs WRs.

predictions.prediction: Woody Marks top-20 PPR RB in Wk7 (must start).
Josh Jacobs over 11.5 carries in his return (Sal's own bet).
Braelon Allen top-12 PPR RB (void if Breece plays).
Jeanty finishes outside the top-17 PPR RBs in Wk7.
Aaron Jones Sr. top-11 PPR RB.
Bucky Irving finishes outside the top-13 (concern call).
RJ Harvey under 5 catches in Wk7 (checkdowns evaporating).
Allgeier out-snaps Bam Knight.
Emanuel Wilson outscores Zach Charbonnet (void if Charbonnet inactive).
Kendre Miller outscores Alvin Kamara.
Jordan Mason top-24 PPR RB (his "could rise" call).
Chuba Hubbard top-12 again (streak continues).

takeaways: Start Woody Marks anywhere you have him; Montgomery is Out per Sleeper and Sal calls Marks a must-start at HOU -9.5.
Breece Hall check before 1 PM: Sal ranks Braelon RB12 on the assumption Breece sits. Sleeper still lists Breece Questionable. If Breece is ruled out, Braelon is a clear start.
Don't flex D-tier RBs over solid WRs. Sal's line: anything in RB25-33 projects ~8-9 points and he'd rather play WRs like Wan'Dale Robinson.
Jeanty is a sell after this week, not a bench, at RB17 with a +4.5 spread.
Jacobs straight back into lineups as an RB2/flex in a 52.5-total game.
Stashes: Tyrone Tracy Jr., Mike Washington Jr., Sione Vaki, Kaelon Black, Emmett Johnson. Droppable: Tyjae Spears.
Mason is a late riser if he practiced fully Friday (Sleeper shows no injury tag Sunday morning).
my_notes:
**MAIN LEAGUE (Myles High Club), your record 2-4**
- **Jonathan Taylor (starting):** Sal's RB8, brutal matchup @ MIN but "obvious starter." Keep him in.
- **Ollie Gordon II (starting):** Sal ~RB21, the "eat my words" guy at only +4 @ NYJ. Fine as an RB2.
- **Jordan Mason (starting, flex):** Sal had him RB33 on Thursday but said a full Friday practice would lift him to ~RB20. Sleeper shows no injury tag and projects him **9.6** (RB29 there). Playable.
- **Kendre Miller (starting, flex):** Sal RB26, "desperation flex," and says he'd rather start WRs over this tier. Sleeper projects **8.9**. Your bench WRs are **Keon Coleman (BUF bye), Stefon Diggs (WAS bye) and Caleb Douglas (MIA @ NYJ)**, so Douglas is the only healthy, playing alternative. With BUF, WAS and LAC on bye, Miller is probably your best option anyway. Your call, Poncho.
- **Omarion Hampton (bench):** LAC is on bye; not in Sal's ranks.
- **David Montgomery (bench):** Out per Sleeper. That's why Woody Marks (on BakedShady's team) is a must-start.
- Opponent-side notes: Freddy (FreddyB2) has **Bijan** (RB3) and **Saquon** (RB14, Questionable hamstring per Sleeper, MNF).

**DYNASTY (SCLSU Mud Dogs), your record 3-3**
- **Kenneth Walker III (starting):** Sal's RB4 despite the SNF revenge spot @ SEA and a KC team total of 20. Start.
- **Breece Hall (starting) vs Braelon Allen (bench):** This is the big one. Sal expects Breece **not** to play and has Braelon RB12 (16.1). Sleeper still says Breece **Questionable (quad)** and doesn't project him in its top 50 RBs, while Braelon projects **15.4**. If Breece is inactive at ~11:30 AM ET, swap Braelon in. NYJ hosts MIA at 1 PM.
- **Rico Dowdle (bench):** Sal RB34, only a play if PIT stays close. Leave him on the bench.
- **Justice Hill (bench):** Sal ~RB38-41. Bench.
- **Isiah Pacheco (bench):** IR; Sal doubts he returns this year.
- Any lineup changes need your OK, Poncho; nothing has been changed.

title: Week 7 Start Sit Advice (Part 2) | Sneaky Starts & Players to BENCH | 2026 Fantasy Football
summary: Friday's Part 2 start/sit show (Adam, Jamey, Dave) recapped TNF, which checks out in Sleeper: Rhamondre 22.5 on one long catch, Swift's third straight 17+ game, Caleb's second straight 300-yard game, and Loveland's 12 targets. It then went through the six NFC home games. Dave was the contrarian: he's down on Dak, A.J. Brown's speed, Tanner McKee and Waddle, and up on Jacobs (about 15 touches), Bryce Young, Purdy as QB6, and Jaylin Noel as the top replacement WR. Jamey backed Jameson Williams, Pitts, Kraft, Dobbins and Waddle, and said to grab Mumpfield if Puka sits. For you, Poncho: Breece Hall is Questionable today, so check inactives and start Braelon if Hall is out. Egbuka is officially out. The hosts liked CAR, SF and DEN as streaming defenses over your beat-up Rams. Freddy's MAIN lineup starts a questionable Saquon, and his dynasty roster lines up well with this show's calls (Noel, Bernard, Mumpfield if Puka sits).

title: Week 7 Mailbag Q&A! Start/Sit, Waivers & Questions Answered! | 2026 Fantasy Football Advice
hosts: Dan Schneier. Producer Sam Davis cameo (judge on the Lord of the Rings bet).
summary: A loose, fun Friday mailbag (Adam's holey socks, Dan losing 3–0 on pop culture, Braveheart homework) with real football in between. The calls that aged best: **sell Nico Collins** (Dan and Jamey; he scored 2.6), Zay Flowers as "this year's JSN" (27.7), Braelon Allen if Breece sat (19.4), Penix or Geno over Shough, Burden's ceiling (23.7), and McConkey over Tyson. Misses: LaPorta over Jacobs, "sit Corum," and benching Omar Cooper Jr. (22.5). Dan: Sell Nico Collins now while there's value. Grade: Nico's ROS PPR PPG < his Wks 1–6 PPG.

Jamey (likely): Emmett Johnson is "the single best stash" and a possible "league winner." Grade: Emmett Johnson an RB3+ (top-36 PPR) for any 3 weeks this season.
Dan: Luther Burden "clearly has the highest ceiling" of Burden/Pickens/Jamo/Shaheed/Higgins. Grade: Burden's best single game ROS ≥ the others'.

Panel: McConkey over Jordyn Tyson ROS. Grade: McConkey ROS PPR points > Tyson.
Dan: CeeDee Lamb > Bijan ROS. Grade: Lamb ROS PPR PPG > Bijan.
Panel: Bucky + Higgins > Breece + Pickens ROS. Grade: combined ROS PPR points.
Jamey: Garrett Wilson won't be limited two straight games. Grade: Wilson ≥ 12 PPR in Week 7. Already ❌ (2-26, 4.6).
Dan: Jahan Dotson is a fine flex "at times." Grade: Dotson ≥ 10 PPR in 2 of Wks 8–11. (Wk7: 1.6.)
Adam: He's more worried about Chase Brown than the panel. Grade: Brown ROS RB PPG rank worse than RB15.

takeaways: Sell Nico Collins (if you can still get WR2 value). Dan and Jamey both said sell before Week 7; he then put up 2.6.

Stash the RB lottery tickets over known roles. Emmett Johnson, Keilan Robinson and Mike Washington over Kendre Miller or Emanuel Wilson types (Jamey, likely). Mine: Wilson just ran for 100 and a TD and Charbonnet is Out, so keep Wilson while Charbonnet is out.
Zay Flowers is a locked-in WR1 with Lamar. Don't sell him for Coker-type pieces.
Don't buy A.J. Brown. The panel walked back their buy-low.
Burden is a ceiling flex, especially with Kmet hurt (23.7 in Week 7).
Overpay for RBs: RB is "dry… after like 13 or 14 guys."
Dynasty (Dan): your late picks are worth less than you think; trade them for players if you're contending.
In 1QB leagues don't trade WR depth to upgrade QB, even for Allen.
McConkey over Tyson in any swap.

title: 9 League-Winning Players to carry you into Fantasy Football playoffs
hosts: solo. Usual co-host Ryan Heath was out (Jacob says he was sick earlier in the week
missed the recording slot; Heath "back next week").
summary: A Jacob Gibbs solo trade-target show. His nine-ish league winners are Parker Washington, Jordan Mason, the cheap Dolphins (Ollie Gordon, Caleb Douglas, Chris Bell), Jeremiyah Love, Ashton Jeanty, Bhayshul Tuten (his loudest call, RB1 the rest of the way), Drake London, Zay Flowers and Tucker Kraft. For you: in MAIN you already own Mason, Gordon and Douglas, and Chris Bell is sitting on waivers. In DYNASTY, hold Douglas, and musicm45 owns Bell, Tuten and Washington if you want to shop.

segments.title: Intro: solo show, Ryan Heath out; "no parameters, no rules," so Drake London is allowed
#1 Parker Washington (JAX): bye-week buy, schedule, Jaguars offense metrics
Cheap version: Jakobi Meyers; "you want at least one Jaguar"; trade ideas (Golden, Olave, Watson for Washington)
Jacob's ROS WR board: Washington WR10
#2 Jordan Mason (MIN): outside-zone scheme, rush success rate, YAC, schedule; ROS RB21
#3-5 cheap Dolphins: Ollie Gordon II, Caleb Douglas, Chris Bell
Caleb Douglas film notes and separation data; Chris Bell as an "A.J. Brown" comp
Break
#6 Jeremiyah Love (ARI): injury, FantasyPros consensus drop, Cardinals offense stats
#7 Ashton Jeanty (LV): efficiency slump, Raiders non-QB production, late schedule
#8 Bhayshul Tuten (JAX): ROS RB11, role growth, route rate spike
Break
#9 Drake London (ATL): WR7 ROS, trade packages, CeeDee Lamb as a sell-high idea
London with Penix splits; Zay Flowers (BAL) split and WR6 ROS
Tucker Kraft (GB): last buy window, two-year TE profile
Wrap: slow starts off injuries should have been expected (Kraft, Jeanty, Love, Tuten); Zay and London have injury/QB discounts

disagreements.Elsewhere: Thursday (SS7) both BTBS hosts said "Oh yes" to Odunze + Mason for Tuten

disagreements.Jacob here: RB19, possible single digits vs LAR

disagreements.Elsewhere: Dan Schneier on Thursday: "I'm out on that" at TE6

disagreements.Jacob here: Sell for Kraft plus (NYG QB worry)
disagreements.Elsewhere: Dan on Thursday: TE5, keep riding

takeaways: Tuten is Jacob's top buy (ROS RB11, says RB1 the rest of the way). His bye is now (JAX Week 7), the classic buy window. Week 8 vs IND is flagged as a breakout spot.
Parker Washington is a bye-week buy too (ROS WR10). Offer Golden-, Olave-, or Watson-type WRs who've scored more.
Zay Flowers (WR6) and Drake London (WR7) are "shouldn't be gettable but might be." Lamb is a sell-within-a-month idea before his rough Weeks 12-16.
Kraft before Sunday: the soft DET matchup could close the window.
Love and Jeanty are patience buys for contenders with depth. Jeanty may be cheaper after another dud this week.
Cheap/waiver darts: Chris Bell, Caleb Douglas, Jakobi Meyers, Chris Rodriguez (Tuten insurance).
Mason (ROS RB21) has the easiest playoff path: DET, WAS, NYJ in Weeks 15-17.

title: Here's What I'd Do with the 10 Most Confusing Players Right Now
summary: On Friday morning the BDGE rankings host (very likely Nick Ercolano, based on the video description) went through fantasycalc's 10 most-traded players. His buys are Josh Jacobs, Michael Wilson and Egbuka (as a buy-low), plus Coker if anyone's down on him. He's holding Ollie Gordon and Chase Brown (leaning buy). His sells are Saquon ("as clear as day"), Hampton and Pickens (hold/sell), and A.J. Brown is now sell/hold after a second TNF dud, a day after Thursday's rankings had him as Feels Good. Every box-score number he gave checked out against Sleeper. For Poncho, that means keep starting Gordon and Coker on Taylor Snift and sell Hampton for anything. Freddy is starting Saquon against Taylor Snift today.

segments.title: Intro: buy/sell/hold on the 10 most-traded players from fantasycalc
1. Ollie Gordon II (MIA RB): HOLD
2. Chase Brown (CIN RB): HOLD, "much closer to a buy"
3. Saquon Barkley (PHI RB): SELL ("as clear as day")
4. A.J. Brown (NE WR): SELL/HOLD ("definitely not a buy")
Arena Club slab-pack rip (Drake Maye blue/orange shock /35, gem mint 10) + promo
5. Michael Wilson (ARI WR): BUY
6. George Pickens (DAL WR): HOLD/SELL
7. Josh Jacobs (GB RB): BUY ("very much a buy")
8. Jalen Coker (CAR WR): HOLD, buy if anyone's down on him
9. Emeka Egbuka (TB WR): BUY LOW
10. Omarion Hampton (LAC RB): SELL ("no chance I'm buying")
Recap of the 10, "once a month" trade video, BDGE Off Center pack-ripping channel, Sunday Twitch stream

disagreements.text: A.J. Brown: Thursday's WR rankings (BDGE-4) had him Feels Good; after the TNF dud he's now sell/hold. That's a real step back from 24 hours earlier, and he says so ("I was kind of unsure").
Josh Jacobs: consistent with BDGE-3 ("right back into the role"), and that's still the open H2H-1024-8 row against Jamey Eisenberg's sell-high.
Michael Wilson: consistent with BDGE-4 (start Wilson over Waddle).
*Mine:* Chase Brown "closer to a buy" goes against the market (he's on the most-traded list because people are selling).

predictions.prediction: Josh Jacobs is a bell cow, 20+ touches a game, with all the goal-line work (17:10).
Samaje Perine does not out-snap Chase Brown going forward (4:42).
Michael Wilson becomes ARI's top WR again; "great wide receiver two" ROS (14:08).
Egbuka has a good second half as a borderline WR2/3 (20:32).
Saquon is a sell; his value drops if he flops on MNF vs DAL (5:23).
Ollie Gordon gets 15+ touches in good matchups, about 11–13 points a week (2:41).
Hampton doesn't get a 70% touch share; the split stays (21:53).
A.J. Brown is not his 2023–24 self (9:04).

takeaways: Jacobs is the buy of the list. In MAIN he's on Amon Raw, Next Question's *bench* right now; that's a manager who might sell. In DYNASTY he starts for Texas Rattlesnake.
Sell Saquon before MNF if you can. He's Questionable (hamstring) and plays Monday. Freddy is starting him against Taylor Snift today.
Hold Ollie Gordon and Coker (both on Taylor Snift). Neither gets you fair value in a trade.
Sell Hampton for anything. He's on Taylor Snift's bench in MAIN.

Buy-low list: Michael Wilson (The Ginyu Force in MAIN, Mcbrid-al Carry in DYNASTY), Egbuka (Killa Walleye in MAIN, ConanWanderer's bench in DYNASTY), Chase Brown (motownmatt in MAIN, Jurgens Off in DYNASTY).
A.J. Brown: don't buy. He's on motownmatt (MAIN) and Chuba Chuba Choo Choo (DYNASTY).
my_notes:
**Taylor Snift (MAIN, vs Freddy's Flowers for Ms. Jackson this week)**
- **Ollie Gordon II** (START, RB): his call is HOLD, a low-end RB2 or flex ROS. Keep starting him.
- **Jalen Coker** (START, WR): HOLD "without a doubt." Keep starting him at CAR vs TB.
- **Omarion Hampton** (bench, RB): SELL. Any return is fine; he's not helping you from the bench.
- **Caleb Douglas** (bench, WR): he says MIA's weapons are fully healthy out of the bye, which helps Douglas and Gordon.

**Amon A Boat! (DYNASTY)**
- None of the 10 are on your roster. Related: **Caleb Douglas** and **Malik Willis** (bench) benefit if MIA's offense improves as he expects. Don't buy A.J. Brown or Saquon from Chuba Chuba Choo Choo.

**Freddy (FreddyB2)**
- **MAIN, Flowers for Ms. Jackson (2-4), your Week 7 opponent:** he's starting **Saquon Barkley** (Questionable, hamstring, MNF). The host's "flop vs Dallas" scenario would help you. If Saquon plays well Monday, *mine:* Freddy will feel good about him, which makes it a bad time to trade for him.
- **DYNASTY, The Man in Jahmyr:** starts **Tetairoa McMillan** (he says CAR's passing game is condensed between McMillan and Coker, a plus) and has **Kendrick Bourne** on the bench (named as stealing targets from Michael Wilson).

title: Sal Vetri: "5 Players You Need to Trade Away Before It's Too Late" (Week 7 sell-highs)
summary: Sal's sell list is five main names (Jeanty, Metcalf, RJ Harvey, Egbuka, Worthy) plus quick spike-sells (Tucker, Pitts, Corum, Omar Cooper Jr.), all under one rule: sell only for real value. His strongest calls are Harvey (81st ROS, receptions-only role) and Worthy (98th ROS, upside gone when Rice is back). For you, Worthy stays in your MAIN lineup this week with Rice out and becomes a sell after; in dynasty, Rodgers' volume is the thing to watch. Captions badly garbled names (Jeanty showed up as "Zamir White" and "Najee Harris," Germie Bernard as "Jerry Jeudy"), and every fix is flagged above.

Jeanty: shop him only for a clean upgrade (Kyren, Watson, Javonte, Parker Washington); otherwise hold.
Tucker, Pitts, Corum, Cooper: "sell-the-spike" pieces; fine as add-ons in two-for-ones.
Egbuka: a split call; hold unless someone pays a top-50 player.
Rodgers volume is a regression risk for every PIT pass catcher.

title: Sal Vetri: "Answering Your Week 7 Fantasy Football Questions" (Thursday live Q&A)

On Freddy's side, Sal would sell his DK and Jameson Williams and is all-in on his Zay Flowers and Gibbs.

- **Core philosophy, stated again and again:** Don't do one-for-one swaps that don't change your lineup. Don't give up the best player in a deal for three fillers. Roster context beats the trade calculator ("the trade calculator can't put your team into it").
- **Confidence (1-5):**
  - 5: Don't trade Kenneth Walker; take Gibbs for Chase Brown + DeVonta ("do this deal yesterday"); keep Watson over AJ Brown; Woody Marks over everyone listed; Josh Jacobs over Harvey.
  - 4: Rhamondre over Mason; fade Christian Kirk; hold Hampton through the bye; keep Jeremiyah Love in dynasty; Montgomery out of his top 100.
  - 3: Likely over Loveland; Nico + Nabers over Bernard; Burden's snap count fine; Puka likely sits.
  - 2: Boston vs DeMario Douglas (flipped mid-answer); Vele vs Boston (hedged); Javonte + Amon-Ra for Gibbs ("I could be wrong there," said three times).
- **Bullish:** Woody Marks, Kenneth Walker, Gibbs, Zay Flowers, Matthew Golden, Christian Watson, Josh Jacobs, Braelon (if Breece is out), Mumpfield (if Puka is out),…

summary: Thursday's Part 1 start/sit show (Adam, Jamey, Heath) covered the seven AFC home games. **Jamey's loves:** Braelon Allen (start of the week if Breece sits), Kyler Murray, Metcalf and Germie Bernard. **Heath's above-consensus picks:** Roschon Johnson (busted on TNF, under 2 points), Kirk Cousins as a top-12 QB, and Pat Freiermuth on National Tight Ends Day. **Avoids:** Mahomes (both, hard), Michael Wilson, the Saints RBs, Charbonnet, Keenan Allen and Loveland. Heath's Loveland fade lost: 19.9 on TNF. Most of the stats checked out against Sleeper (Kamara/Miller touches, Bernard's 21 targets, Flowers' Huntley games, Mayer, Washington, Watson), with a few misses (Rodgers' "four straight 20+," Concepcion's floor). For you, Poncho: in DYNASTY, **if Breece Hall is ruled out, start Braelon Allen**, the hosts' start of the week. In MAIN, you're stuck with Mahomes at QB with Josh Allen on bye, Kendre Miller is the starter the hosts like least (Hampton is on your bench), and the Jets DST is the hosts' preferred stream over your Rams. Freddy's MAIN lineup is mostly players the hosts like (Rodgers, Metcalf, Flowers), and Barkley is "expected to play."

takeaways: If Breece Hall sits, Braelon Allen is a must-start (Jamey's start of the week; Hall didn't practice Wed; Sleeper lists Hall Questionable). Both hosts take Braelon over Chase Brown if Hall is out.
Get away from Mahomes if you have a real alternative: Gino, Kyler, Rodgers, Stafford, Stroud, Purdy all ranked over him by at least one host. Rashee Rice is Out per Sleeper.
Start both Steelers WRs (Metcalf slightly ahead of Bernard), and Jaylen Warren as a borderline RB1. Rodgers is a usable QB12.
Fade Shough, the Saints RBs, Michael Wilson (if Surtain plays), Keenan Allen vs MIN, and the Giants RBs.

Chase Brown is a start by default, but watch his workload split with Perine. Perine is the better stash than Roschon now that Monangai is expected back.
Charbonnet: both hosts lean him over Emanuel Wilson as a flex for the TD equity, but Sleeper still shows him Out (ACL/PUP tag). Check before lock.
TE: Kelce is a low-end TE1; Freiermuth a low-end starter (Heath's sleeper); Higbee over Mayer over Parkinson.
Streaming D: Jets (vs MIA) and Bengals (if Huntley starts) over the Rams; avoid the Steelers DST.
Waiver: Christian Kirk (Evans not expected, Deebo missed) and Fernando Mendoza in Superflex.

summary: A tight 44-minute Thursday rankings show (Jamey, Dave, Heath) going position by position with starts, sits and sleepers. Dave had the best week: Judkins (23.4), Caleb Williams (22.12), Warren, sit both Vikings backs, Loveland as a top-12 TE (19.9) and the Davis Allen nudge (18.0). Heath's big swings missed: Roschon as a near-RB2 got 2 carries, Bryce Young as near must-start threw 2 picks (7.42), and he sat Jacobs (20.1). Jamey's WR starts (Bernard, Metcalf, Kirk) all flopped, but his Braelon Allen start and Mahomes bench hit. For you: put Diggs back in for Week 8, keep Judkins and Pitts rolling in SUPERFLEX, consider Caleb Douglas over Waddle, keep Jacobs and Swift in HEROES, and play Rachaad White in DYNASTY now that he leads WAS.

predictions.prediction: Jamey: Stefon Diggs is "a borderline must start wide receiver starting in week 8 and beyond." Grade: Diggs top-30 PPR WR in Weeks 8–11.
Jamey: Antonio Williams is a must-add with McLaurin out for the season. Grade: Williams top-36 PPR WR in 2+ of Weeks 8–11.
Jamey: Chig Okonkwo "going to be very prominent in the passing game" for WAS. Grade: Okonkwo 5+ targets/game Weeks 8–11.
Jamey: Terrance Ferguson "could be a big difference maker until Davante Adams returns." Grade: top-12 TE in any week he plays before Adams returns.
Heath: Carnell Tate is "a top 24 wide receiver… most weeks." Grade: top-24 PPR WR in 3+ of Weeks 8–12. (Wk7 9.9.)
Dave: Kyle Pitts is a mid-season bounce-back as a short-area TE. Grade: Pitts top-12 PPR TE PPG for Weeks 7–12. (Wk7 13.2.)
Dave: Bryce Young (with Heath) is a near must-start QB with McMillan and Coker healthy. Grade: Young top-12 QB in 3+ of Weeks 8–12. (Wk7 7.42.)
Jamey: Geno has a "revenge game" vs LV in Week 8 and the whole Jets passing game "could be fun." Grade: Geno 20+ and a Jets WR 15+ PPR in Week 8.
Dave: Kirk Cousins could be benched for Fernando Mendoza "if they continue to lose." Grade: Mendoza starts by Week 10.
Dave: Loveland is a top-12 TE going forward when Caleb plays in structure. Grade: Loveland top-12 PPR TE in 3+ of Weeks 8–12. (Wk7 19.9.)
Heath: Malik Washington "might score two or three" TDs and is "absolutely… a top 36 wide receiver." Grade: Washington top-36 PPR WR PPG Weeks 7–12. (Wk7 6.5.)
Jamey: Week 8: Jadarian Price returns and the SEA backfield gets "really messy." Grade: Price active Week 8 and no SEA RB over 60% of snaps.

takeaways: Diggs is back in lineups from Week 8 (Jamey: "borderline must start"), and Antonio Williams and Chig Okonkwo are the WAS pickups with McLaurin out for the year.
Stash Terrance Ferguson on IR if you have a spot (Jamey). He won't be back for Week 8.
Lean on Dave's usage reads over Heath's projections for now (mine: in the Week 7 grades above, Dave's calls mostly hit and Heath's big swings mostly missed).
Judkins is a locked-in RB2 (Dave; 23.4 in Week 7). Braelon Allen stays a flex even with Breece back (Jamey).
Loveland is startable: Dave's top-12 call was right (19.9), and he's the TE with real target volume (12 in Week 7, mine).
Fade the Colts passing game while Daniel Jones is this bad (Heath; Downs 3.8, Allen 6.1, Jones 4.62).
Geno over Penix-type streamers in Week 8 (Dave), with the LV revenge game (Jamey). Mine: Geno scored 24.48 in Week 7.
Don't trust Bryce Young as must-start yet (both hosts said yes; 7.42 with 2 INTs).
Watch Jadarian Price's return in SEA before trusting Emanuel Wilson again, even after his 18.5 (Jamey).

title: Week 7 Rankings I Start/Sit I Fantasy Football Advice
summary: Thursday's BTBS start/sit show was Jacob's full Week 7 rankings plus chat Q&A. Both hosts were all-in on Jordan Mason, endorsed Aaron Rodgers hard, and made Braelon Allen's value hinge on Breece Hall. The Thursday results went their way on Swift, Stevenson, Loveland, Burden and Maye, while the Pop Douglas hype (5.3 PPR) and AJ Brown (7.8) missed. For you: Mason is a start in MAIN, Kendre Miller is shaky but your bench is thin, and in DYNASTY you should check Breece Hall's status before 1 PM and pivot to Braelon if he's out. Hockenson is active and endorsed.

segments.title: Intro: Thursday = listener-question show; BTBS Sicko dynasty league trade talk ("insulting offer = no counter")
TNF preview: Caleb vs Drake Maye, Patriots O-line worries, Vegas (CHI 4th-highest implied total, NE 14th)
RB rankings (Swift RB8 & the Roschon usage correction; JT RB10; Saquon/Pierce; Breece/Braelon; Mason vs Aaron Jones; Jeanty; NE/DEN/ARI backs; mixed backfields; Seattle/Charbonnet; Henderson)
Break
WR rankings (CeeDee Lamb vs Fangio, Golden WR7, Nabers slot rate, Coker vs T-Mac flip, AJ Brown, Pickens, Mingo, PIT WRs, Pop Douglas separation, Keenan vs Downs, Evans/SF flyers)
Break
TE rankings (Kittle w/o Evans, LaPorta, Likely TE5, Kraft "out on that", Hockenson, National Tight End Day, Freiermuth birthday)
QB rankings (Purdy QB1, Lamar QB2?, Maye over Caleb, Stroud, Kyler QB10, Shough, Rodgers' game log, Bo Nix QB15, McCarthy)
Chat Q&A: start/sit, flex calls, trades (Likely trade-tier ladder, Odunze + Mason for Tuten)
Outro

disagreements.Jacob: Prefers Pierce/Rhamondre/Aaron Jones over a hamstring Saquon

disagreements.Who's right so far (mine): Pop: 3-23, 5.3 PPR Thursday ❌ for Dan's hype
Burden 23.7 already banked; Mason pending Sunday

disagreements.Jacob: Could break out vs DET's weak secondary
Bucky is a bet on role regardless

disagreements.Dan: Lamb and Pickens both fine vs Fangio

takeaways: Jordan Mason is both hosts' favorite RB start of the week (RB17, IND at home, MIN -6.5). Healthy per Sleeper now.
Breece Hall decides Braelon Allen: RB12 if Breece sits, ~RB20 for both if he plays. Breece is Questionable (quad) per Sleeper.
Start Aaron Rodgers over Shough/Nix/Cousins; QB8, QB3, QB12, QB13 the last four weeks, PIT -3 vs NO (9:30 AM ET kickoff, ESPN line).
Hockenson is a "Hock it up" start vs IND (Dan).
Keenan Allen is only WR41; he's a full-PPR floor play ("six for 38"), not a ceiling play.
LaPorta TE4 vs GB in the week's highest total (53.5).
Kendre Miller is RB28 and depends on Kamara sitting; Kamara is healthy on Sleeper now, so Miller is a fragile flex.
Waiver-ish: Germie Bernard (WR23-24, ~8 PPR floor), Pop Douglas (already flopped Thursday), Charbonnet (stash for after the Wk11 bye).
Trades: both hosts would do Odunze + Mason for Tuten; Likely is worth roughly AJ Brown / DeVonta Smith / Tuten / Chase Brown, not Pickens, Michael Wilson or Mike Evans.

title: BDGE: "Ranking Every Week 7 Wide Receiver as a Sit or Start" (Week 7 WR tiers)
summary: BDGE's Thursday Week 7 WR rankings (same unnamed solo host as Wednesday's RB video, 32:50) put every WR into five tiers. TNF went half his way: Luther Burden (23.7 PPR) and the low-floor Pop Douglas (5.3) and Kalif Raymond (0) calls hit, but his Feels Good A.J. Brown laid a 7.8 and NE's targets spread out instead of condensing. Both of his injury reads are now Sleeper "Out" tags (Egbuka, Rashee Rice). His Sunday calls to watch are CeeDee going "nuts," the Metcalf/Bernard target share, Carnell Tate and Denzel Boston as strong dub flexes, Michael Wilson over Waddle, and Adonai Mitchell over Omar Cooper. For Poncho, Coker (Feels Good) and Amon-Ra (Must Start) look good. The flags are Worthy in MAIN (only a shaky flex even with Rice out) and Shaheed in DYNASTY ("rather not shaky flex"), and neither has an obvious bench upgrade. Freddy is starting Mumpfield ("floor is a zero") and a Lamar-less Zay Flowers.

Trust the Must Start list: Olave, Nabers (expect a dip), Nico, Chase, Higgins, Jefferson, Garrett Wilson, London, Amon-Ra, Watson, Golden, Puka (Questionable, calf), JSN, CeeDee.
Pittsburgh's pair is the best dub-flex value: Metcalf and Bernard vs a "terrible, terrible" NO defense.
Young CLE/TEN receivers over the vets: Carnell Tate and Denzel Boston are dub flexes, and Jeudy/Ridley are Rather Nots.
Jets slot: if Adonai Mitchell is active, start him over Omar Cooper. Both are only shaky flexes.
Keenan Allen over Josh Downs if you have to start a Colt vs the MIN defense.

summary: Hayden's Week 7 half-PPR RB top 40 starts Gibbs, CMC, Bijan, Henry, Walker. His biggest stands are Woody Marks at RB10 (consensus RB19, "fringe RB1" with Montgomery out), Swift at RB7, and a late drop of Jonathan Taylor to RB12 at Minnesota, the toughest RB matchup in the league. TNF already graded several calls. Swift (19.0 PPR), Luther Burden (23.7), Loveland (19.9) and Rhamondre (22.5) all hit. His live swap of Roschon Johnson over Pollard missed (1.3 points). The stats they cited mostly passed the Sleeper check, but a few were slightly off: Chuba was RB13 once in half-PPR, Swift's no-Monangai run was RB8, and Pierce was RB14 last week. For you, Poncho: JT is still a start but with lower expectations. In DYNASTY, Hayden expects Breece to sit and ranks Braelon RB11, so swap him in if Breece is ruled out. Jordan Mason off IR is the riskiest of your MAIN flexes.

takeaways: Hayden's Woody Marks call (RB10, consensus RB19) is the big swing. Montgomery is Out ✅ and Jawhar Jordan is Out ✅. HOU's team total is 26.25 and they're 10-point favorites over McCarthy's debut. His actual scoring has been RB22-23 the last two weeks, so this is a bet on game script.
TNF mostly backed Hayden. Swift ✅ (19.0 PPR), Burden ✅ (23.7), Loveland ✅ (19.9) and Rhamondre ✅ (22.5) all hit. His one live change, Roschon over Pollard, missed badly (1.3).
JT is a lower-end RB1/RB2 this week at MIN (12.7 RB pts/g allowed, the fewest ✅; IND team total 17.5). It's not a bench, but expectations are lower.

The injury report changes a few of his assumptions. Lamar is Out (Henry's "markets assume Lamar" premise), Saquon is Questionable (Pierce RB17 only if Saquon sits), Breece is Questionable (Braelon RB11 only if Breece sits), Love is Out and Charbonnet is Out (Emanuel Wilson's ceiling goes up, not down).
Matchup wins: Warren vs NO (most RB pts allowed ✅), Braelon vs MIA, Gordon vs NYJ, Pierce vs DAL.
Matchup fades: Kendre at PIT (10 red-zone trips allowed), JT at MIN, Pollard vs CLE (2nd-fewest RB pts ✅), Walker at SEA (still RB5 on volume).
Backfields to avoid: NYG (Skattebo RB33/Tracy RB34, "Nothing is locked in"), SEA, ARI (Bam Knight over Allgeier if anyone), DEN (Dobbins over Harvey).

Stats that failed the Sleeper check: Chuba's worst week was RB13 in half-PPR (RB12 in PPR). Swift's no-Monangai run was RB8 (not RB5). Pierce was RB14 last week (not RB15). Ollie Gordon has 1.0-1.25 catches per game (not 1.3). Mason and Jones's W1 snap shares were 45%/46% (not 47%/43%). Everything else they cited checked out ✅ (Gibbs's 28/g, JT's 4.0 YPC and 38/24 catches, Javonte's 6 TDs in 4, Judkins's RB21/RB8/RB30, Kyren's five 10%+ target-share games).

title: Sal Vetri: "7 Players About to GO NUCLEAR in Fantasy (Trade For Them Now)" (Week 7 buy-lows)
summary:
Sal's Week 7 buy-low list has eight names. **DJ Moore** is his favorite buy at any position (33% target share in two healthy games, back from the bye in Wk8), and **Chase Brown** is next (the fumble cost him Wk5, but CIN's offense is top 10). He also wants **Jaylen Warren** (74% snaps with Dowdle back, a top-15 RB ROS), **Woody Marks** as the cheap one (78% snaps, Montgomery out), and **Zay Flowers** and **Christian Watson** if a losing team will panic. **Ladd McConkey** ("it feels gross") is a stash-buy, and **A.J. Brown** is a "significant buy low" who then went 3/48 on TNF. For Poncho, nothing forces a lineup change before Sunday. The best angles are trades: A.J. Brown from 0-6 cdurka55 in DYNASTY, and DJ Moore or Chase Brown from motownmatt in MAIN.

---
*Queue: Sal also posted RWMuTkTZGqQ "5 Players You Need to Trade Away Before It's Too Late," 7y6AFsWTrOw "My Week 7 Running Backs Rankings and Tiers," and hA_6llL2d40 "This News Changes Everything (Week 7)" (Sat 10/24). They're next, one per run.*

takeaways: DJ Moore is Sal's #1 buy. He's on bye and still listed Out, so his price is at its lowest now. Pay a Jameson Williams or Michael Wilson-type piece.
Chase Brown is #2. The fumble-driven Wk5 split and the Wk6 bye made managers sour. He's back Wk7 @ BAL.
Jaylen Warren is a hold-or-buy. 74% snaps with Dowdle back says he's the lead. Dowdle is now Questionable (knee) too.
Woody Marks is the cheap buy. Montgomery is Out for Wk7, the matchup flips from JAX to NYG at home, and the 78% snaps / 61% routes role is safe. Ignore Jawhar Jordan's TD (and he's now listed Out).
Test the market on Flowers and Watson. Send offers only to 0-6, 1-5 or 2-4 teams. Note Lamar is still listed Out for Wk7.
McConkey is a stash-buy for Wk8+. Out (concussion) and on bye; the price only goes up once he clears protocol.
A.J. Brown: Sal says buy, TNF says wait. He went 3/48 with another drop. If his owner panics, that's the window, but it's a riskier buy than Sal sold it.
