title: Buy Low & Sell High Trade Targets Ahead of Week 7  | 2026 Fantasy Football Advice
hosts: Jamey Eisenberg (joined ~3:10). Dave Richard was off ("Dave won't be here today").
summary: A Wednesday buy-low/sell-high show with Adam, Heath and Jamey. **Buy:** Bucky Irving (Heath) and DJ Moore (Jamey), plus Drake London, McConkey and A.J. Brown. **Sell:** DeVonta Smith (Heath) and Josh Jacobs (Jamey); the hosts' own team flipped Jacobs for Saquon Barkley on air. **Hold:** the Packers WRs and Bowers. Adam's Likely and Giants-QB stats checked out perfectly against Sleeper (TE1, 9.8 targets a game, 5 TD; Giants QBs 324 yds/g, 8 TD, 5 INT, 43.3 att over three games). The TNF calls mostly hit: Maye, Caleb, Henry, Burden, Loveland and Swift did, while A.J. Brown, Douglas and Heath's Roschon pick didn't, and Jamey beat Heath on Rhamondre (22.5). For you, Poncho: in MAIN, Coker is a start and LaPorta is the TE1 you'd want, Freddy's Barkley is the injury to watch, and both hosts preferred Caleb to Freddy's Rodgers. In DYNASTY, the hosts like your bench back Braelon Allen over Breece, Bowers is a hold, and you should re-check Hockenson. Freddy left 34 TE points (Loveland 19.9 and Henry 14.1) on his dynasty bench Thursday.

title: WR Rest of Season Rankings I Week 7 Fantasy Football trade targets
hosts: solo ("a little bit short-handed this week"). Dan Schneier
not on the show. The tight ends are folded into this episode because there's no separate TE
summary: Jacob's Wednesday WR update is all usage. He moved A.J. Brown up to WR20 despite a 5.7-point game (22 XFP), raised Golden to WR14, dropped Garrett Wilson to WR18 and Michael Wilson to WR24, and called Coker and McMillan studs who help each other. Omar Cooper Jr. was his top waiver WR, Germie Bernard has a high-floor PPR role, and Christian Kirk and Ja'Kobi Lane are his stashes. For you, Coker and Worthy are both backed in MAIN, and Kirk and Lane are free. In dynasty, Shaheed is the shakiest start by his data, with Kupp the higher-floor bench option, and Odunze is a hold he's lukewarm on.

segments.title: Cold open: deep-target leaders (Golden 14, Olave 13, Metcalf 12, Nabers 10); Mike Evans deep-target spike
A.J. Brown's 22 XFP vs 5.7 FP; Matthew Golden and route depth (the 9-yard rule)
Marvin Harrison Jr.'s HOU debut alignment (press rate); C.J. Stroud's catchable air yards
Catchable air yards, Week 6: DeVonta Smith, Nabers, Omar Cooper Jr.; Cooper vs Pop Douglas
Week 6 XFP leaders: Germie Bernard, Pop Douglas, Egbuka, Josh Downs, Zay Jones, Luther Burden, Rome Odunze
Break
ROS WR rankings walkthrough (WR1-~13 shown on screen only; WR14-54 read aloud)
Break
Team-by-team usage: WAS, TEN, TB, SEA, SF, PIT, PHI, NYJ, NYG, NO, NE, (MIA/MIN bye), LAR, LAC, LV, KC, JAX, IND, HOU, GB, DEN, DAL, CLE, (CIN bye), CHI, CAR, BUF, BAL, ATL, ARI
Bonus slot-rate notes: Nabers 41%, CeeDee Lamb 40%+ three straight
Deep stashes: Christian Kirk, "De'Shawn Shrubling" ❓; close

disagreements.text: No in-episode disagreements (solo show). He invites listeners to flip several pairs: Coker or McMillan up to the Nabers line, DeVonta Smith over Pickens, Metcalf over Waddle.

Cross-episode drift (BTBS vs BTBS): in this 10/21 episode Parker Washington sits just above Pickens (around WR12-13 by his description). Two days later, in the 10/23 "9 League-Winners" episode, he had Washington at ROS WR10 and Zay Flowers at WR6. Flowers here is only "extremely excited" inside WR1-13. Track both in the LW and WR7 rows.
Self-flagged tension: he ranks Waddle (WR27) over Metcalf (WR30) while admitting Metcalf is getting the role he wants for Waddle.

takeaways: Buy A.J. Brown on the 5.7-point game. 22 XFP is the biggest XFP-minus-FP gap for any WR game since 2021 in the FP Data model, with a 94% route rate in his first game back.
Hold or buy both Panthers WRs. Coker and McMillan's slot rates have converged (~37% each), and Jacob says they help each other.
Omar Cooper Jr. was his top waiver WR, with Germie Bernard right there (back-to-back elite XFP, 12 of 12 targets catchable).
Sell Garrett Wilson high if someone still pays a top-10 price. He's down to WR18 because the injuries that boosted his target share are healing.
Michael Wilson and Egbuka are usage-over-production buys, but Jacob trimmed Wilson to WR24.
Waddle at WR27 is a hold, not a dump; if you need points now, Jacob is fine flipping him for Diggs or someone in that range.
Avoid: DEN (except as a hope play), TEN beyond Tate, IND beyond Keenan Allen, SF WRs other than Evans, Mumpfield, Kupp and Barner outside deep leagues.
Cheap stashes: Christian Kirk (SF), Ja'Kobi Lane (BAL), Devontez Walker (BAL), Caleb Douglas (MIA), Ryan Flournoy (DAL), Harold Fannin Jr. (dynasty buy-low).
TE notes: Isaiah Likely is a WR in TE clothing; a Tucker Kraft bounce-back is "coming"; Loveland has been unlucky; Jake Ferguson's 50% route rate is a red flag.

title: RB Rest of Season Rankings I Week 7 Fantasy Football trade targets
hosts: solo. Dan Schneier is referenced but not on the episode.
summary: Jacob's Wednesday RB ROS update is all usage. His big movers are Tuten (now ahead of Jeanty), Hubbard (up 5 to RB10) and Kyren (RB8 and climbing). Charbonnet is his cheap sleeping-giant bell cow, and Mason is his favorite "points now" back. He's down on Jeanty's health, Jacobs (RB25), Rhamondre, Akers, and the DEN, NO, NYG and WAS backfields. For you, Mason, Ollie Gordon and JT are all backed. Kendre Miller is the weak link in your MAIN lineup. In dynasty, keep an eye on Breece Hall's status, with Braelon Allen behind him.

segments.title: Intro: a "Breeland" (Tuten) victory lap; show schedule (Tue and Thu 11 AM ET live with Dan Schneier; ROS rankings every Wednesday, one position at a time)
Running back analysis: Tuten's metrics, JAX run game, Chris Rodriguez
Usage deep dive: Zach Charbonnet's sleeping-giant case; Chuba Hubbard and Tuten as risers
Role trends: route participation and XFP leaders from Week 6
ROS rankings walkthrough, RB1 to about RB56
Break
Team-by-team usage, ARI through LV
Break
Team-by-team usage, LAC through WAS
Closing

disagreements.Other side: Dan Schneier "didn't feel like it was totally over" (relayed, 25:27)
The consensus market ("maybe that's too low," he concedes)

disagreements.Note: Same as the LW ep (Tuten RB11)

disagreements.Other side: Matches his SS7 stance vs Dan ([H2H-1024-3])

takeaways: Bhayshul Tuten is Jacob's top RB buy. Past-2-weeks XFP is RB7, Jeanty's snaps are fading, and LV's bye is late. He moved Tuten ahead of Jeanty.
Chuba Hubbard: ride him (ROS RB10). He played 93% of snaps with a 69% route rate, and the offense is now built around him.
Kyren Williams has a top-3 RB role on paper (#2 in XFP/g over 4 games). With Davante Adams out, the role may grow.
Zach Charbonnet is a cheap stash with bell-cow upside once he's back from the ACL. Jacob expects him to pass Rhamondre quickly and doesn't see Jadarian Price getting the valuable work.
Jordan Mason over Judkins and Saquon now. Ollie Gordon II gets the same nod. Aaron Jones loses value with Mason back.
Sell or fade Jeanty at name value unless his health turns. Rank Swift next to him.
Treat Jacobs as an RB3 until Green Bay's backfield shows it can produce.
Bucky Irving's value depends on Tampa's offense. The role (85% snaps) is good.
Stash Rico Dowdle and Travis Etienne Jr. (NO, IR). Ignore the DEN, NYG, NO (Kendre Miller is TD-only) and WAS backfields.
Dameon Pierce is a Week 7 flex (RB18 vs DAL MNF) only if you have to start him.

title: BDGE: "Ranking Every Week 7 Running Back as a Sit or Start" (Week 7 RB tiers)
summary: BDGE's Wednesday Week 7 RB rankings (solo, 28:39) put every back into five tiers. TNF already went his way: Swift (19.0 PPR) and Stevenson (22.5) hit, and Henderson, Kiner and Roschon flopped like he said. His Sunday calls to watch are Kenneth Walker going "nuts" vs SEA, Allgeier over Knight, Jacobs straight back into his role, and Jordan Mason held to 8-10 touches behind Aaron Jones. For Poncho, the flag is Jordan Mason in the MAIN lineup (only a shaky flex here). Walker, Taylor and Ollie Gordon look good, and Braelon Allen is the swap if Breece Hall sits in DYNASTY. Freddy has Pierce as cover if Saquon misses.

takeaways: Trust the volume backs: his Must Start list is Swift, Warren, Henry, Bijan, CMC, Chuba, Bucky, J. Taylor, Gibbs, Kyren, Kenneth Walker, Javonte. TNF already backed up the Swift and Stevenson calls.
Don't rush Jordan Mason back. He sees 8-10 touches and has Aaron Jones as the better (dub flex) start. That matters for Poncho's MAIN lineup (see below).
Breece Hall is the swing: if he plays he's only a dub flex, and Braelon Allen drops to shaky. If he sits, Allen "feels good." Wait for the Sunday inactive list.
Ollie Gordon and Woody Marks are confident starts in good matchups.
Avoid the Giants backfield completely, and don't trust any SEA back (Charbonnet is now Out anyway).
Allgeier over Knight in Arizona, while Love is out.
Jacobs: start him if you have him, but expect inefficiency behind a bottom-two OL.
Stash Dylan Sampson in deep-bench leagues.

summary: Josh Norris and guest Joel Smyth called this "the worst waiver wire of the season" (34:49). Their top add is **Omar Cooper Jr.** (51 of 62 snaps, WR6), then **Ja'Kobi Lane** (red-zone role) and **Jaylin Noel**. For you, it backs the Cooper bid in MAIN and keeps Kendre Miller in your Week 7 flex.

takeaways: Omar Cooper Jr. is the top add (#1 for both hosts). He played 51 of 62 snaps, and Josh thinks he can take Adonai Mitchell's job. Josh would bid 10-12% of budget, and Joel less than that.
The three "obvious" adds come first if they're free: Tre Tucker (WR2 in Week 6), Germie Bernard and Malik Washington.
Ja'Kobi Lane is #2: a red-zone receiver who gets better when Lamar returns. Josh would only go 5-10% FAAB.
Noel is #3: efficient and catches everything, but he's only on half the snaps.
RBs are thin. Kendre Miller is a stash (bye in Week 8, then a soft schedule), Mike Washington is a Jeanty handcuff, and Zonovan Knight is outplaying Allgeier. Avoid the Giants backfield.
Michael Mayer is a real TE streamer: LV is in 2-TE sets 66% of the time, the most in the league.
Superflex: McCarthy for the rest of the season, McKee as a one-week play vs Dallas.
Drops: Tyreek Hill, Jonathan Brooks, Makai Lemon and BTJ (in redraft).

url: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=br_2VGAYcw8 · Runtime: 2:26:46 (finished livestream) · Sponsors: Farmers Insurance ("fantasy breakdown" read at 35:29, Rams segment), DraftKings (promo read at 1:17:45)
summary: Josh, Hayden and Matt Harmon ran their 2½-hour Week 7 Stats vs. Film. Hayden's re-draft top six is Gibbs, Walker, Bijan, JSN, Puka and Amon-Ra. The biggest calls: buy George Pickens after the Eagles game, start Tyler Higbee as a top-12 TE with Adams out, add Antonio Williams (Hayden), Omar Cooper (Matt) and Travis Hunter, and avoid the Giants and Seahawks backfields. TNF already graded a few of them. Loveland was "for real" (7/12-69-1), Hayden's "complicated" NE backfield read beat Kiner hype (Rhamondre 22.5 PPR, Kiner 1.3), and Hayden's Jeremiyah Love return call is dead (he's Out). One cited stat failed the Sleeper check: Lawrence's "19+ in 13 straight." For you, the episode backs keeping Kendre Miller, Mason, Worthy and Coker in MAIN. In DYNASTY, watch Breece's quad (Braelon is the fallback), and Keenan Allen looks like your weakest starter.

title: Sal Vetri: "5 Players I'm Panicking About in Fantasy Football" (Week 6 panic meter)
summary: Sal's Week 6 panic meter rates seven players. **Full panic** on **Cam Skattebo** (0 carries, 6 snaps, benched for fumbles; bench every Giants RB) and **Jaylen Waddle** (a 30% target share wasted by Bo Nix's 4.0 Y/A and 4.9 aDOT). **No panic** on **A.J. Brown** (97% routes, 10 targets, drops; "set for a big Thursday Night Football") and **Jaylen Warren** (74% snaps; Dowdle's hot first half was "fear-mongering"; top-15 RB ROS). **Moderate** on **Josh Downs** (needs 10 targets in a checkdown offense), **4/10** on **Bucky Irving** (elite role, no efficiency), and **7/10** on **Michael Wilson** (screen-heavy, tough schedule; Bourne is a flex add). For Poncho: Sal calls **Tyler Warren's** groin a likely multi-week absence, so swap **Keenan Allen** into that DYN slot, and fill MAIN's empty FLEX with **Kendre Miller**.

segments.title: Cold open: whether to panic, "full on panic," or make a move
Cam Skattebo / Giants backfield: 0 carries, 6 snaps, fumbles, Glazer's "Najee starts" report, five-RB committee. Full panic
Jaylen Waddle / Bo Nix: 30% target share for 4/24, aDOT 4.9 joke, WR52, 646-yard pace, Payton's quote. Full panic
Recording-time note (Mon noon ET); R.J. Harvey's checkdowns
A.J. Brown: 97% routes, 34% target share, 2-4 drops (a likely 60-yd TD), Doubs AC joint → "big Thursday Night Football." No panic
DraftKings ad
Josh Downs: no Pierce or Tyler Warren (late scratch, groin), Keenan Allen's 12 targets, game log since Pierce's injury, Daniel Jones' struggles. Moderate panic
Subscribe ask ("over 60%… are not subscribed")
Bucky Irving: 21 touches for 49 yards, 85% snaps / 90% rush share, backup QB, Baker's thumb, last year's 10.2 PPG split. 4/10
Ad for his free start/sit tool (fantasyfootballstarts.com): Mike Evans 17.2 vs Terry McLaurin 11.2 projection demo
Jaylen Warren vs Rico Dowdle: first-half 54% Dowdle opportunity share was "fear-mongering"; final 74% snaps, 66/33 carry split. No panic
Michael Wilson vs Kendrick Bourne: 4 of 7 targets were screens, McBride's NFL record, Bourne's 64 yds / 8 targets as a starter, tough schedule. 7/10
Wrap and plug for his waiver video

format: Solo panic-meter video. Each player gets a panic grade, sometimes as a number (Bucky 4/10, Wilson 7/10), with a built-in "it depends on your expectations" hedge for Downs, Bucky and Wilson.
tone and emotion: Disgusted and sarcastic about the Giants and Broncos ("disgusting" about seven times, "Sure." at Harbaugh's denial, the Bo Nix name joke). Protective of A.J. Brown and Jaylen Warren, calling the Warren panic "fear-mongering for no reason." Measured on Bucky.
bullish: A.J. Brown ("big Thursday Night Football"), Jaylen Warren (top-15 RB ROS), Kendrick Bourne (bye-week flex), Bucky's role, Rodgers' passing volume.
bearish: Cam Skattebo and the whole Giants backfield (no adds, no trades, no starts), Jaylen Waddle and Bo Nix ("this offense is broken"), Josh Downs and the Daniel Jones checkdown offense, Michael Wilson as a WR2, R.J. Harvey's checkdowns.
method notes: Route % vs target share (Brown 97% / 34%, Waddle 80% / 30%), snap and rush share (Bucky 85/90, Warren 74/63/55), first-half vs full-game splits (Dowdle), game logs with a big game removed (Waddle ex-Wk2), "points left on the field" from drops (~7 for Brown), and schedule strength (Wilson's next 5).

Jaylen Warren is a top-15 RB rest of season, not top-5 (grade: PPR RB rank Wks 7-17)

Waddle can't be started; nothing changes under Bo Nix (grade: Waddle outside top-36 PPR WR Wks 7-10 = hit)

Bucky Irving is a "matchup dependent RB2 / flex," not an elite RB (grade: RB13-30 PPR Wks 7-10 = hit)
Michael Wilson ranks WR20-30 weekly, a WR2/3 flex (grade: avg PPR WR rank Wks 7-11)
ARI's next 5 (DEN, DAL, SEA, LAR, KC) give Wilson only one good matchup (DAL) (grade: Wilson's best game is vs DAL = hit)
Tyler Warren's groin is "usually a multi-week absence" (grade: misses Wk7 and Wk8 = hit)

takeaways: Bench every Giants RB, Skattebo included, and don't add Tracy, Najee or Singletary. Sal wouldn't trade for any of them either.
Don't start Jaylen Waddle in Bo Nix's offense (aDOT 4.9, 4.0 Y/A). Hold him in 12+ team leagues; he's droppable only in shallow 10-teamers.
Start A.J. Brown with confidence in Wk7 (97% routes, 10 targets, Doubs likely out). It's Sal's most confident call.
Keep starting Jaylen Warren (74% snaps). Dowdle's first half was noise, so Dowdle is a handcuff, not a flex.
Bucky Irving = RB2/flex, not a sell-in-a-panic. The role is elite, but efficiency is capped until Baker is healthy.
Downgrade the Colts' WRs under Daniel Jones. Downs needs 10 targets, and Keenan Allen only pays in PPR when he catches 7-8+.
Tyler Warren may miss multiple weeks (groin). Plan around him.
Michael Wilson is a WR3/flex with a tough next five. Kendrick Bourne is a live bye-week flex add.

title: FFT Dynasty report: 8 Cheap Contender BUYS + Injury Replacements (Week 6 Dynasty Recap & Reaction)
summary: Heath and Alfredo built a contender shopping list priced mostly in 2nds and 3rds. Alfredo is high on Tyler Shough, done with Bo Nix (QB20), and would take Caleb over Daniels without hesitation. Gordon is a better rental than Marks, Jacobs and Charbonnet are too risky at a 2nd, and Pitts beats Henry and Freiermuth. With McLaurin probably done, Antonio Williams is the buy and Diggs could be a league winner. Tucker, Noel, Tank Dell and Keon Coleman are all fades or stashes, while Keenan Allen's volume is worth a late 3rd. For you, the big things are three Out players in your Week 7 DYNASTY lineup (Hall, Hockenson, Warren), Diggs and Keenan Allen gaining value, and two 2027 3rds that line up with 0-6 cdurka55's Freiermuth and Shakir.

takeaways: Contender price list (both hosts): a late 2nd buys a rental RB (Gordon, Marks) or MHJ; a 3rd buys a fill-in TE (Henry, Freiermuth) or Shakir; a late 3rd or 4th buys Keenan Allen; two 3rds for Tucker; a 2nd + 3rd max for Terrance Ferguson; a late 2027 1st buys A.J. Brown, Higgins, DeVonta Smith, Pickens if available, or Coker.
Washington WRs: with McLaurin probably done, Diggs is the No. 1 and Antonio Williams is the breakout buy (his rookie value is dipping, −181 FC in 30 days).
Don't pay 2nds for Jacobs or Charbonnet: legal and suspension risk (Jacobs) and a crowded SEA backfield (Charbonnet, still on PUP in Sleeper).
Sell Travis Hunter for a 2nd and Woody Marks at RB2 prices (Alfredo); sell or avoid Bo Nix.
Waivers: Christian Kirk is the top deep add; Tyrone Tracy is worth a cheap bid after the Najee cut; don't chase Jaylin Noel's 15.9 YPT.
Tank Dell: keep stashing; don't start him.
Tre Tucker over Keon Coleman, but neither is worth a 2nd.
Superflex only: Dak is a QB1 buy (maybe wait a week); Watson is two 2nds max for a desperate contender; hold Tanner McKee rather than take a 3rd.

title: Who to Add for Week 7? Waiver Wire Targets, Streamers & Must-Have Pickups | 2026 Fantasy Football
summary: A 44-minute Tuesday podcast (Adam, Jamey, Dave), separate from the morning livestream. **Rachaad White** is still the #1 add despite the bye. **Omar Cooper Jr.** is Dave's WR pick and Jamey's long-term pick, and **DeMario Douglas** is the better Week 7 start. Jamey streams **Kyler Murray** and **Rodgers** "right away," while Dave would start **Kirk Cousins** over both. At TE it's **Hunter Henry** (Jamey) vs **Kyle Pitts** then Higbee (Dave). Dave says cut **MarShawn Lloyd** for **Pierre Strong** and grab **Tyrone Tracy** if White is gone, and **Kendre Miller** is again a "trap back." Adam's tip: **Will Reichard** is 15-for-15. Dave won "Who Has More?". Nearly every stat checked out against Sleeper; the one miss was Adam's Concepcion "9, 8, 6 targets in his last three" (Week 5 was 1). For you, Poncho: in MAIN, Cooper, Douglas, Henry, Pitts, Murray and Reichard are all free, and your starter Kendre got called a trap again. In DYNASTY, you own White and Rodgers, and Douglas, Murray, Tracy and Pierre Strong are free. Freddy starts MarShawn Lloyd (the show's top drop) and has Henry, Ferguson, Reichard and Gibbs rotting on his bench.

title: Week 7 Waiver Wire: MUST ADD Players, Injury Replacements & Streamers | 2026 Fantasy Football Advice
summary: A 69-minute Week 7 waiver show with Adam, Jamey and Dave, one day after Jamey's 50th. **Rachaad White** is the consensus #1 add despite the Wk7 bye (low-end RB2 for three games, up to 20% FAB). **Omar Cooper Jr.** (~15%) and **DeMario Douglas** (<10%) are the WR adds; Douglas is the better Week 7 start and Cooper the better hold. At TE, Jamey wants **Hunter Henry**, Dave wants **Michael Mayer** and a **Terrance Ferguson** stash, and **Kyle Pitts** is the upside play. **Kyler Murray** and **Rodgers** are the streaming QBs, the **Browns** the top DST, and the **Kendre Miller** fight ends with "only if you're desperate." Every stat checked against Sleeper held up except Jamey's McLaughlin goal-line TD (it didn't happen in Wk6) and a couple of small counting slips. For you, Poncho: MAIN has a bye-week hole (Hampton plus an empty slot) and Cooper, Douglas, Pitts, Henry and Murray are all free there. In DYNASTY, Hockenson and Warren are both Out, so pivot to Keenan Allen. Freddy is hoarding Henry and Ferguson on his DYNASTY bench, and his MAIN starters (Cousins, Juwan, Vele) got roasted.

Freddy's Zay Flowers got the biggest hype, but it all depends on Lamar's ankle.

my_notes:
**MAIN, Taylor Snift (PPR + first downs; 70.75 in Wk7 so far).** You're starting Kendre Miller (Jacob's top waiver RB; 5.8 so far) and Xavier Worthy (a riser for both, but KC's implied total is just 20 at SEA). Jalen Coker got Dan's "massive win" nod (1.9 so far). Omarion Hampton on your bench is a "role up, don't buy" guy, so he's a hold, not a starter. Stefon Diggs (bench) gets the red-zone and third-down "souped-up Downs" role now that McLaurin is out, which fits first-down scoring once WAS is off bye. Davante Adams on IR opens the Rams door for Mumpfield and T. Ferguson (Ferguson is now on IR too, per Sleeper).

**DYNASTY, Amon A Boat! (full PPR; 57.28 so far).** Rome Odunze (10.9 on TNF) is the guy both hosts said has too few chances. Rodgers (13.08 so far) was Jacob's second-tier stream, and Dan leaned Geno. Kenneth Walker is on Dan's "wouldn't trade for CMC" list. Tank Dell on your bench is expected to be eased in (Jacob said about 5 routes); he has 1 catch for 43 yards so far. Trevor Lawrence (bench) was Wk6's QB1, and Dan says JAX's run and pass games are finally clicking. Quentin Johnston and Brenen Thompson are on the team Dan called "totally shot." Breece Hall being out has helped Braelon, and Jacob ranked Braelon top-12.

**Yahoo HE-MAN'S HEROES.** McConkey (Out) is a faller for both. D'Andre Swift's role didn't change without Monangai, though Roschon took 40% of snaps (Swift had 19.0 on TNF). Josh Jacobs is "top-20 easily," but Pierre Strong may take passing downs. Herbert on your bench: Dan is "out on Herbert."

**Yahoo He-Man's New Super Flex.** Waddle has slid to Jacob's WR3 range. Penix (19.88 so far) was a hard "no" from Dan. Pitts (bench, 13.2 so far) isn't a buy for Dan. Lamar should be back soon, which they say boosts Zay Flowers.

title: A Week to Take Advantage of Your Idiot Leaguemates on Waivers
summary: Michael O'Hara's Week 7 BDGE waiver show says the RB pool is "really brutal" and the value is at WR and TE stashes. His top stash is Terrance Ferguson, followed by Jonah Coleman, Travis Hunter and Dylan Sampson, and Keenan Allen and DeMario Douglas are his plug-and-play flexes. He's cooler than the market on Omar Cooper Jr. ("more of a bench stash") and Mumpfield, and he says to drop BTJ, Sutton, Lloyd and Keaton Mitchell. For Poncho, the show supports the DYNASTY claims on Kyler and Douglas and says to flex Keenan Allen. In MAIN it's a mild caution against raising the Cooper bid. Freddy owns both of Michael's favorite stashes (Ferguson and Sampson), and two of his starters (Lloyd and Sutton) are on the drop list.

segments.title: Intro. "If you need a running back this week, good luck because it's really brutal"
QB targets: C.J. Stroud (0:30), Kyler Murray (0:45), Michael Penix (2:09)
Superflex QBs: Tanner McKee (4:17), J.J. McCarthy (5:26)
RB targets: Roschon Johnson (6:59), Kendre Miller (9:50), Jaleel McLaughlin (12:25), Dylan Sampson (13:54), Tyrone Tracy (14:58), Samaje Perine (16:57), Jonah Coleman (18:15)
WR targets: Omar Cooper Jr. (20:15), Keenan Allen (22:13), Travis Hunter (23:13), Jaylin Noel (25:33), Ja'Kobi Lane (27:27), Konata Mumpfield (28:33), Antonio Williams (30:18)
WR "roster band-aids": DeMario Douglas (31:48), Brandin Cooks (33:14), Christian Kirk (34:41)
TE targets: Tyler Higbee & Hunter Henry (35:21), Terrance Ferguson (36:04), Chig Okonkwo (38:06), Michael Mayer (39:06)
Trending drops: MarShawn Lloyd, Keaton Mitchell, Jacory Croskey-Merritt, Emanuel Wilson (RB); Darius Cooper, Courtland Sutton, Brian Thomas Jr., Dontayvion Wicks (WR)
Outro

disagreements.Details: Michael: "more of a bench stash," won't out-target Garrett Wilson, and Adonai Mitchell muddies it. FFT's Jamey called him the "headliner," Hayden says every 12-team league, and Poncho's MAIN plan bids $121. Nick (BDGE-1) was also "hesitant," so BDGE is consistently cooler
#3 trending add (+410k on Sleeper per the 10/20 waiver intel); Michael: "not as much of a slam dunk" because of 13 personnel; 5–7% FAAB
Michael: don't let 18.5 PPR fool you; Skattebo's benching is "a slap on the wrist." Dan (FFT) was bullish; Sal called it fool's gold, which matches Michael
Michael: Skattebo likely "leads the backfield next week." Nick (BDGE-1): "You just got to take the L"

Michael: "the primary ball carrier… moving forward," but "not that good." FFT: "clear goal-line back." Nick (BDGE-1): three-way split. Michael is the most bullish BDGE voice on role, and the least bullish on talent
Michael: return "as early as this week" and a real job threat. Nick: gets rolling around Wks 9–11
Michael: stash, everything moving his way. Sal: "too valuable on defense." (Matches Nick's add)
Michael: stash him right now, the #1 TE pickup. Nick: only if Adams misses multiple weeks (Adams is now out 6–10 weeks, so Nick's condition is met)

predictions.take: Skattebo "comes back and leads the backfield next week" (Wk 7)
Terrance Ferguson becomes "basically… the wide receiver 2 behind Nacua" once he returns (eligible Wk 8)
Jonah Coleman challenges and can "straight up steal" Dobbins' lead job
Dylan Sampson is CLE's 1A over McLaughlin and Estimé whenever he's active and Judkins sits
Kendre Miller stays NO's primary ball carrier until Kamara is healthy
McCarthy is named NYG's starter "soon"
Omar Cooper won't out-target Garrett Wilson week to week ("No chance")
Keenan Allen keeps a 9+ target floor, especially with Warren out
Jaylin Noel's role expands from his 51% route rate
Mumpfield's role is limited by heavy 13 personnel without Adams
Mike Evans misses Wk 7
Brian Thomas Jr. stays droppable, with no fantasy-relevant role unless traded
DeMario Douglas is a usable short-term flex until Brown, Hollins and Doubs are back

takeaways: Terrance Ferguson (LAR TE, on IR): Michael's #1 stash ("go stash him on your IR slot right now"), and Adams is out 6–10 weeks.
Jonah Coleman (DEN RB, IR): the strongest RB stash; Dobbins is at 3.3 YPC ✅.
Keenan Allen is "the epitome of a spot start in your flex": 9+ targets for three straight games ✅, more if Warren sits.
DeMario Douglas is a short-term flex on TNF @CHI (19.6 and 22.5 PPR in Wks 5–6 ✅).
Kyler Murray is the 1QB streamer for the soft stretch (IND, DET, BUF); Penix is a coin-flip stream vs SF.
Stashes: Travis Hunter, Dylan Sampson (free), Ja'Kobi Lane, Antonio Williams, Jaylin Noel, Perine.
Spot RBs only if desperate: Roschon (6–8% FAAB, TNF), Kendre Miller, McLaughlin. Avoid Tracy.
Cooper Jr. is a bench stash with WR2 upside vs MIA; don't expect him to out-target Garrett Wilson.
Drops: BTJ, Sutton, Lloyd, Keaton Mitchell, Croskey-Merritt (IR), Emanuel Wilson, Darius Cooper, Wicks.
my_notes:
**MAIN LEAGUE: Taylor Snift (Poncho)**

**DYNASTY: Amon A Boat! (Poncho)**

**Freddy, MAIN: Flowers for Ms. Jackson**
- **Keaton Mitchell** (bench): "an easy drop."
- **Saquon / Pierce:** McKee is PHI's QB for the year, with "really, really poor" efficiency, which hurts the whole PHI offense.
- **Kirk Cousins:** Michael expects LV to "rack up some pass volume" vs LAR (the Mayer section). **Bijan:** the Penix TD coin-flip cuts into Bijan's goal-line TDs. **Zay Flowers:** Lane is lining up as the WR2 behind him once Lamar returns. **Vele / Juwan Johnson:** the NO offense "has not been effective." **Jakobi Meyers:** JAX is pushing its depth WRs (BTJ) out. **Jaguars DEF:** not discussed.

**Freddy, DYNASTY: The Man in Jahmyr**
- **MarShawn Lloyd** (his RB starter): "easy drop" now that Jacobs is back. That's the second show today to say so.
- **Terrance Ferguson** (his bench, IR): Michael's #1 TE stash, so Freddy owns the guy this show wants most.
- **Dylan Sampson** (his bench, IR): Michael's preferred CLE back once he's active. Another Freddy win.
- **Courtland Sutton** (his starter): "Straight up awful… easy drop."
- **Hunter Henry** (his bench): worth a pickup. **Fannin / Raheim Sanders:** CLE's backfield goes McLaughlin → Sampson. **Kyren / Corum / Stafford / Ty Simpson:** LAR goes heavy 13 personnel without Adams. **Jaxson Dart (IR):** NYG might hand McCarthy the job. **Addison:** a Kyler "cupcake" stretch helps. **Deebo (Out):** Evans is out too, so Cooks and Kirk soak up routes.

takes.detail: "Rostered in 60% of sleeper leagues… The guy has straight up been hooping"

Completion rate "pretty high," but production and efficiency lag. "Cupcake schedule coming up" (IND, DET, BUF D's "outright horrific"). Wk 5 vs NO: 51 rush yds ✅ (24/30, 229, 1 TD, 10 car). Best in Wks 8–9 when opponents force dropbacks

ATL scoring well with him (claims ~45 vs GB, 23 vs BAL/CHI; team scores not checked). 1 pass TD in each of his first three starts ✅ (Wks 3–5), then 3 TDs vs CHI in catch-up mode ✅ (225 yds, 23.1). TD split vs Bijan / B-Rob is "a scratchoff lottery ticket." Wk 7 vs SF should force dropbacks

Starter "for either the entire season or the foreseeable future"; Hurts (blood clots) expected out for the year. First start: 45 att ✅, 26 cmp ✅, 215 yds ✅. EPA/play "really, really poor" ❓. Wk 7 vs DAL is "attackable"

243 yds, TD, INT ✅. "17 fantasy points in the fourth quarter" (Sleeper total 17.32 ✅; the Q4 split isn't checkable). Played "roughly 11 minutes." Doesn't change his long-term view ("larger sample… just frankly horrible"), but Harbaugh "has a decision to make"

Monangai has missed 2 straight; estimated DNP Monday on a short week (TNF vs NE). ~40% snaps both weeks ✅ (27/69, 31/77). Wk 5: 7 tgt, 5 rec ✅. Wk 6: 13 car ✅, 2 tgt ✅, TD ✅; 8 of 13 carries came in Q4 garbage time, and he went down at the 1 to ice it. "It's a gross one"

Travis Etienne on IR. Since Kamara's back injury: 44.4% snaps ✅ (32/72) and 20 carries ✅ in Wk 6; 4 of 5 inside-the-5 carries over two weeks ❓. YPC 3.0 / 3.5 ✅. "He's not that good," but "15 carries, 75 yards… and punches in a score" is the serviceable story. Primary ball carrier "until either [Etienne] returns or Alvin Kamara is good to go"
Hurt his back in Wk 4, aggravated it diving for a pass in Wk 6; "they don't want to just ram [him] into the line." Watch practice
Lead back with Judkins out: 63% snaps ✅ (39/62), 9 car ✅, 4 tgt ✅. Lost the lone goal-line carry to Aaric Estimé; "5'7, 187 pounds." Wk 7 @TEN is "relatively stout"
Limited practices last week before being ruled out; "just straight up a better player" than McLaughlin or Estimé. "My preferred option in deeper leagues… the 1A should Judkins miss." Get him for $0

Skattebo benched: 6 snaps ✅, 0 touches ✅. Snaps: Tracy 30 (Sleeper 29 ⚠️), Singletary 26 (Sleeper 31 ⚠️), Harris 11. 8 touches ✅, 45 scrimmage yds ✅, 2 TDs ✅, 38% snaps ✅, 18.5 PPR ✅. "I'm not going to let the box score… play too many tricks on me"
"Most likely it was a slap on the wrist. He comes back and leads the backfield next week"
CIN had a Wk 6 bye. Wk 5: 14 car ✅ at 4.8 YPC ✅ (68 yds) with goal-line work. "8% rostered" ❓. 1A/1B or handcuff value

Dobbins "3.3 yards per carry" ✅ (270 yds on 81 carries). "His job is anything but safe." Coleman could be back "as early as this week"; "one of the few situations where… a rookie… just straight up steal[s] someone's job." Stash in IR

Wk 1: one route, 30-yd catch ✅, then ankle sprain and IR. Wk 6 return: 82% snaps ✅ (51/62), 81.8% route rate ❓, 23.3% target share ❓, 7 tgt ✅, 0.26 TPRR ❓, 6/103/1 ✅ (48-yd TD from Geno). Won't out-target Garrett Wilson ("No chance"); Adonai Mitchell's return "further muddies the waters." Could start vs MIA, "but I think this is more of a bench stash"

url: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lJQPIjlEJus · Runtime: 1:45:19 · Sponsors: Farmers Insurance, DraftKings (promo segment ~0:26, ~0:50)
summary: Josh, Hayden and Matt Harmon went through all 11 Sunday-afternoon games in 1:45. Their biggest calls: JJ McCarthy will start more games than Winston ("a guarantee"); Coker and McMillan are top-20 WRs the rest of the way; Omar Cooper Jr. should be rostered in every 12-team league; Pierce's role is too big to fail; and Kenneth Walker (19-128-2) belongs in the OPOY mix. Germie Bernard (11 catches, a Steelers rookie record) is the new PIT WR2. Chargers RBs combined for 43 yards and are unstartable. Kendre Miller owns the Saints backfield. Adams left late with a calf/possible pull, so watch him.

title: 10 Must Add Players to Pick Up in Your Fantasy League Right Now
summary: Sal's Week 7 waiver video is built around **adds vs fool's gold**. The clear #1 is **Germie Bernard** ("100% of my fab"). Next tier: **Ja'Kobi Lane**, who has red-zone equity with Lamar back and Bateman's AC joint hurt, and whom Sal prefers over **Kendre Miller** (20 carries but only 32/72 snaps, Etienne coming). Also **Kendrick Bourne** (bye-week flex), **Omar Cooper Jr.**, **DeMario Douglas** and **Malik Washington**. Stashes: **Dylan Sampson** (expected back Wk7), **Jaylin Noel** (14+ teams), **Bam Knight**, and handcuffs **Kaelon Black / Emmett Johnson / Brian Robinson**. Avoid **Tyrone Tracy** ("let your idiot league add" him), **Travis Hunter** ("too valuable on defense") and **Brian Thomas Jr.** ("unusable"). Don't sell **A.J. Brown** over his drops. Poncho: Sal is fading your Miller and backing this morning's waiver plan. Freddy owns half of Sal's list.

Rookie WR adds: Omar Cooper Jr. (6/100/1, but Gonzalez inflated his share) and DeMario Douglas if Doubs sits. Also Malik Washington (59% available), ahead of Caleb Douglas.
Stashes: Dylan Sampson (expects a Week 7 return), Jaylin Noel (14+ team leagues), Bam Knight (if Love sits), plus handcuffs Kaelon Black, Emmett Johnson and Brian Robinson.
Fool's gold, don't chase: Tyrone Tracy, Travis Hunter, the Giants backfield, and Brian Thomas Jr. ("unusable").
Don't panic-sell A.J. Brown over the drops (34 routes, 10 targets in his return).

title: EARLY Week 7 Waiver Wire TARGETS! Cooper, Tyson, Tracy Jr, Murray, Henry, & Others! (FFT Express)
summary: A 10-minute early waiver episode on Jamey's 50th birthday. **Omar Cooper Jr.** is the headliner, though Adam worries about Adonai Mitchell's return and Garrett Wilson. **DeMario Douglas** is a low-FAB add, **Hunter Henry** is "the easy one" at TE, with **Mayer** behind him. For QBs, **Murray** and **Rodgers** are the Week 7 starters (slight nod Rodgers), and **McCarthy** is a must-add in 2QB/Superflex. RBs got a flat "No," with Tracy, Miller and Knight as the deep options. The **Vikings** are the #1 DST. Every stat checked out against Sleeper. For you, Poncho: the MAIN wire has Murray, Henry, Mayer, Cooper, Douglas and three of the four DSTs, which helps with Allen's bye and Andrews's slump. Freddy has Henry on his DYNASTY bench and Rodgers on his MAIN bench.

title: Week 6 Winners & Losers: Biggest Takeaways From Every Game! | 2026 Fantasy Football Advice
summary:
Four-man Winners & Losers after the 1 PM / 4 PM windows. **Jamey's winners** were waiver darling **Germie Bernard** and **Luther Burden**; **Heath's** were the tight end bounce-backs **Loveland** and **Pitts** (Pitts target share up four straight weeks to 21.2%). **Dave** crowned **Stroud** and **Bryce Young** must-start QBs and buried **Odunze** / **Michael Wilson**. Biggest loser energy: **Skattebo** (zero touches under Harbaugh), **Downs** still stuck, **Rhamondre** after Kiner's clock-kill package, and Adam sweating **Braelon** into **Breece**'s job. Game-by-game they stuck up for **Woody Marks**, framed **Tuten** as a strong RB2 (not RB1), debated whether **Warren** was a missed sell-high, and told 1QB managers to **dump Herbert**. For your rosters: MAIN should be nervous about **Hampton** and curious about **Miller**'s goal-line role; DYNASTY got a spike from **Walker** + **Keenan**, a Dave cold shoulder for **Odunze**, and a reminder that **Braelon**'s production is on a timer once Hall returns.

**Freddy watch:** In DYNASTY, Freddy rostered the show's #1 winner (**Germie Bernard**, Jamey) and Heath's TE winner (**Loveland**). His MAIN QB **Cousins** boomed late (Adam started him in about seven leagues), while **Meyers** (14.3, "better times ahead") and **Henry** (14.8, preferred over Douglas on the wire) scored on his benches. **Kyren Williams**'s "I'm not out there" quote is the one to watch.

title: Week 6 Recap: McCarthy vs Winston, Coker vs McMillan, Jacobs Returns, & More! | Beyond the Box Score
summary: Beyond the Box Score's Week 6 recap was a sell-Jacobs show: all three hosts see him as a touchdown-dependent RB2 behind a bad Packers line, with Green Bay's backfield at just 14.2 expected points per game. They split on the Giants (Dan likes McCarthy's arm, Adam thinks he was lucky), framed Coker vs McMillan as close with Coker riding slot matchups, and rolled out buy-lows led by A.J. Brown, Nico Collins, MHJ, Kraft and Loveland, plus waiver darts Tracy, Noel, Dotson and Flournoy. For you, Poncho, the big news isn't from the show: Davante Adams is out 6-10 weeks, so Taylor Snift needs a WR this week, while Coker looks like a locked-in starter.

takeaways: Sell Josh Jacobs if your league still pays RB1 prices. All three hosts lean sell (GB RBs: 14.2 expected points/game, 32nd in YPC), and one option is to wait a week for a touchdown. [my check] He came off the exempt list Monday and will practice all week, but LaFleur said playing at DET is "to be determined" (USA Today Packers Wire, NBC Sports), and the NFL conduct investigation is still open (WBAY).
Buy A.J. Brown, Nico Collins and Marvin Harrison Jr.; they're the consensus-ish buy-lows with the strongest underlying numbers (catchable air yards, Stroud's 6-for-6 200+ games).
Tucker Kraft at DET is the TE buy of the week (pace for 105 targets, DET worst vs TE).

Woody Marks is a Week 7 start vs NYG if Montgomery sits. [my check] Sources disagree on Montgomery (groin): CBS lists him questionable for Week 7, while StatChasers and Fantasy Alarm call him out or week-to-week.
Free waiver adds: Tyrone Tracy Jr. (best Giants RB on tape), Jaylin Noel (2.53 YPRR), Jahan Dotson (one-on-ones), Ryan Flournoy (95% routes, 4+ targets every game).
Coker vs McMillan is basically a coin flip, with Coker favored in slot-friendly weeks and McMillan facing tough outside corners (DEN, MIN, CIN, SEA).
Watch the Cincinnati backfield: Chase Brown could lose work to Perine based on formation.
Drop Darren Waller. He's out-routed by Tremble and squeezed by Coker.
Bears: Caleb's game was a conservative script (aDOT 3.9), so Burden's 42% route rate is less scary than it looks. Loveland is still a buy.
Avoid Najee Harris and Pickens buy-lows. MarShawn Lloyd is done once Jacobs returns.

title: BDGE: "This is not your grandpa's fantasy football league" (Week 6 game-by-game recap)
summary: Nick's Monday recap goes game by game from TNF through SNF and skips MNF. For Poncho: Walker is a must-start "revenge game," the LAC backfield is unstartable (Hampton), Keon Coleman fades once Moore returns, and Adams' non-contact leg injury has "a wide range of outcomes." Breece is 50/50 for Wk 7. He backs Rodgers vs NO and Jaylin Noel, and he's cooler than others on Omar Cooper and Kendre Miller.

Nick Ercolano.text: Mixes route-share and snap data with what he sees on film and plenty of profanity. He pushes back on overreactions (RJ Harvey's dud was "variance"), but he's also quick to write players off (Skattebo "take the L," Denver's WRs "useless"). He mentions his own leagues often ("your idiot league mates" league: Nico, Woody Marks, Jakobi Meyers, Fannin, Charbonnet). He was early on Kenneth Walker and takes a victory lap for it.

title: FINAL Week 6 Start/Sit Cheat Sheet PART 1! LIVE Q&A + Actives/Inactives News | 2026 Fantasy Football
summary: This was an hour of lightning-round start/sit on what both hosts called the hardest week of the year. Heath was the projection-driven one: Pierce is a top-24 RB at 11.8 projected points in full PPR, and Jordan Love is his QB2. He fades Skattebo (four fumbles in five games), Najee and the WAS committee, and says to drop Lloyd for Cooks because Jacobs starts in Week 7. Adam pushed back on Pierce ("I don't think he's that good"), argued for Keon Coleman, and was skeptical that Germie Bernard could be a league winner, offering Matthew Golden instead. Heath's "preponderance of evidence" line about Coleman was the best exchange. Both hosts would trade Hampton for Burden. TE handling: Strange until news came, then Freiermuth after Rapoport's report. Warren's absence moves Downs and Keenan Allen up.

segments.title: Open. "the most challenging week of the year thus far"; a little wind in PIT @ TB; Heath: "This week is survival of it could be the fittest, maybe the luckiest"
Giants backfield: Dan Duggan reports more Najee; Skattebo's fumbles; Woody Marks over Skattebo
Where Heath ranks A.J. Brown, DeVonta Smith and McConkey. Freiermuth and Warren both GTD, so Heath moves both behind Brenton Strange
Fill-in RBs by team: HOU (Marks), PHI (Pierce), ARI (Allgeier), the CLE/NO messes, WAS ("full-blown committee")
Chat start/sit lightning round #1, with banter: "Am I drunk?", lineup-setting on air, a likes challenge, Adam's three-QB drop dilemma, game of the week

my_notes:
**DYNASTY (SCLSU Mud Dogs):**
- **Jayden Daniels (QB, MNF):** Heath took **Jordan Love over Daniels** ("He's my QB2 this week"). No other Daniels verdict.
- **Braelon Allen (RB):** a clear start for Heath. Allen > Allgeier and Allen > Rhamondre; ≈ Tuten (Adam took Tuten); **Bucky Irving > Allen** (Heath). Kept in every RB/flex set.
- **Brock Bowers (TE):** "I'm going to trust Brock Bowers."
- **Keenan Allen (W/R/T):** Warren-dependent. Keenan is the choice over White if Warren is out, and he ranks ahead of Coleman if Warren is out. Heath picked Worthy over Ladd and Keenan. With Warren **inactive**, Keenan is a flex.
- **Rachaad White (W/R/T, MNF):** Heath: "full-blown committee in a very bad matchup." Lost to Hampton and Vele; beat Kendre Miller; if Warren is out, Keenan beats White. **Since Warren was ruled out, the hosts' logic says start Keenan Allen over White at W/R/T.**
- **Stefon Diggs (WR, MNF):** status unknown; Heath would "wait" if he had Diggs. Have a backup ready.
- **Tyler Warren (bench TE):** Heath benched him for Strange before the news. **Inactive.**
- **Trevor Lawrence (bench QB):** loses to Dak and Cousins, beats Jameis and Stroud, a coin flip with Mahomes. (He already played in London; JAX lost 31-34.)
- **Aaron Rodgers (bench QB):** "I do not trust Aaron Rogers" (Heath). Shough is preferred; Adam would take Rodgers over Jameis.
- **Austin Ekeler (bench):** banged up and in Heath's Rico Dowdle tier. **Rico Dowdle (bench):** "not worth a flex," a possible goal-line role.
- **Quentin Johnston (bench):** Heath picked Johnston over Cyrus Allen, Royals and **Josh Cameron (also yours)** in non-PPR.
- **Amon-Ra St. Brown (bench):** only mentioned as sitting on Heath's bench (DET bye).
- **Caleb Douglas (taxi):** "Douglas" in a sit-two at 57:09 got benched, along with Bourne. It's *probably* Caleb Douglas, but not certain.
- **Breece Hall:** never mentioned by the hosts. *(Guru: inactive, per NFL.com.)*

**MAIN LEAGUE (Myles High Club):**
- **Omarion Hampton (RB):** a borderline RB2. Below Pierce and Pollard; above White; ≈ Kamara. "Ran two routes last week." **Both hosts would trade Hampton for Luther Burden.**
- **Keon Coleman (WR):** the main Adam-vs-Heath debate. Heath has him as a low-end WR3 (low-to-high 30s) and a drop candidate because **BUF has a bye next week**; Adam makes the case for him. *(DJ Moore was inactive.)*
- **Jalen Coker (W/R/T):** in Heath's PPR pick-twos (Coker + A.J. Brown; Zay + Coker). Lost to Jeanty and Pickens.
- **Xavier Worthy (W/R/T):** "could be a decent start" with Rice out (Adam). Over Ladd and Keenan (Heath); under Burden and Tate.
- **Josh Allen (QB):** Adam noted Allen "threw 19 passes" in Week 5. Heath expects a big James Cook run game vs LV, which is slightly bearish for Allen's passing volume.
- **Patrick Mahomes (bench QB):** Maye > Mahomes; a coin flip vs Lawrence.
- **Kendre Miller (bench):** "all he did last week was score a touchdown. It was 10 carries for 30 yards." Behind Kamara. Heath said to drop Strange rather than Miller.
- **Makai Lemon (bench):** "we're not going to go with Lemon" (55:06).
- **Sam LaPorta (bench):** only mentioned as on Heath's bench (bye).
- **Stefon Diggs (bench):** as above.
- **Rams DST:** Adam notes "the Rams are so good against tight ends." *(Guru: LAR −12.5, ARI implied total 19.5, a strong DST spot.)*
